_comment: PER-MARKET DOSSIERS for the international growth cluster.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-international-growth-cluster-design.md
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
Shingle-overlap catches duplication only AFTER a page is written. This file
catches thinness BEFORE. A page may not be written until its dossier is filled,
and verify-cluster-pages.js fails the page if the market-specific facts listed
here are not actually present in the rendered HTML.
RULES
1. requiredMentions must contain at least 8 entries, each a market-SPECIFIC
string: a named statute, regulation, curriculum document, exam board,
institution, dataset, operator or place. Generic marketing words do not
count and defeat the purpose.
2. No string in requiredMentions may appear in another market's dossier.
That is the anti-duplication rule, enforced by the gate.
3. localProject must name a real dataset from that market with a real
analytical trap. This is the strongest anti-duplication device we have.
4. sources must contain at least 3 primary sources, with the claim each one
supports. If a claim cannot be sourced, it does not go on the page.
A claim that resists sourcing gets stated as unconfirmed, or dropped.
The New Jersey entry records a real lesson: the widely repeated claim that AP
computer science satisfies part of a New Jersey mathematics credit could not be
confirmed at primary source, and second-hand accounts contradicted each other on
both the start year and which credit it covered. It was removed from the page.

coding-classes-in-georgia.curriculumAuthority: Georgia Code 20-2-149.3, Requirements for computer science education (SB 108, 2019). All middle schools in a local system must offer instruction in exploratory computer science, including state charter schools serving middle grades. High schools were phased: at least 50 percent of a system's high schools from 2023-24, all from 2024-25. The statute supplies an unusually BROAD definition of computer science, which is the page's second point: two schools can both comply while teaching very different things.
coding-classes-in-georgia.localProject: Base rates and conditional probability, anchored on published CDC prevalence figures, with Atlanta as the home of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Trap: given a positive result from a highly accurate screening test for a rare condition, most positives are FALSE positives, because the small error rate applies to the very large healthy population. Taught as a two by two table of counts for 100,000 people rather than as Bayes' theorem in symbols. Ninth distinct KIND of error. Deliberately distinguished from the Illinois class-imbalance project: Illinois is about choosing the right METRIC for an imbalanced problem, Georgia is about what a positive result actually MEANS once the base rate is known.
requiredMentions: algorithmic processes, coding, and logical thinking

sources.claim: Georgia Code 20-2-149.3 requires each local school system to provide that all middle schools offer instruction in exploratory computer science, and that state charter schools serving middle school students do the same. For high schools the duty is phased: beginning in the 2023-2024 school year at least 50 percent of a system's high schools must offer a course in computer science, and beginning in the 2024-2025 school year all of them must. The statute defines computer science as the study of computers, algorithmic processes, coding, and logical thinking, including computer principles, their hardware and software designs, their implementation, and their impact on society.
sources.citation: Official Code of Georgia Annotated 20-2-149.3, Requirements for computer science education

sources.claim: A student meeting the requirements to be a HOPE Scholar at the time of high school graduation must earn a minimum of four full rigor credits from the Academic Rigor Course List prior to graduating. Computer Science Principles and Games, Apps and Society are among the courses that satisfy HOPE rigor, and Advanced Placement courses in core subjects are approved rigor courses. The list is maintained by the Georgia Student Finance Commission.
sources.citation: Georgia Student Finance Commission, HOPE Scholarship initial academic eligibility and Academic Rigor Course List

sources.claim: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, and publishes prevalence figures for conditions that students can look up directly.
sources.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

rejectedClaims.claim: Georgia's computer science requirement came from HB 897.
rejectedClaims.why: Wrong bill, caught before writing. The requirement traces to SB 108 (2019), codified at O.C.G.A. 20-2-149.3. The initial research assumption was checked against the code section rather than trusted.

rejectedClaims.claim: A specific named test with specific sensitivity and specificity figures.
rejectedClaims.why: The page deliberately describes the screening test in general terms ('correctly identifies almost everybody who has the condition, wrongly flags only a small percentage of those who do not') and has students look up current CDC prevalence themselves, rather than printing invented or unsourced diagnostic accuracy numbers that would date badly and could be read as medical guidance.

coding-classes-in-washington.curriculumAuthority: Washington state computer science learning standards, referenced by RCW 28A.230.300 as the alignment test a course must meet before it can substitute for a third year mathematics or science course.
coding-classes-in-washington.localProject: Seattle Open Data, Fremont Bridge Bicycle Counter, running since October 2012 with hourly counts from inductive loops in the east and west pathways. Two traps, both about CONSTRUCT VALIDITY rather than statistics: (1) one bridge is not a city, so any claim about Seattle cycling drawn from a single sensor is a claim about that sensor; (2) the columns are east PATHWAY and west PATHWAY, not eastbound and westbound, and the loops count bicycles regardless of travel direction, so a commute-direction chart built from them measures which side of the bridge people ride on. Eighth distinct KIND of error: the variable does not mean what its name implies, and nothing was miscalculated. NOTE: no claim about counter outages or missing data appears on the page, because that could not be verified.
requiredMentions: third year mathematics or third year science

sources.claim: RCW 28A.230.300 permits a student to substitute a computer science course aligned to state computer science learning standards as an alternative to a third year mathematics or third year science course. Before approving it, the school counselor provides the student and the student's parent or guardian with written notification of the consequences of the substitution on postsecondary opportunities. The student, parent or guardian, and school counselor or principal must all agree; the substitution must align with the student's High School and Beyond Plan; and each student is limited to one such substitution.
sources.citation: Revised Code of Washington 28A.230.300, Computer science

sources.claim: RCW 28A.230.097 requires boards of directors to approve AP computer science courses as equivalent to high school mathematics or science, and to denote on a student's transcript that AP computer science qualifies as a math-based quantitative course for students who take the course in their senior year.
sources.citation: Revised Code of Washington 28A.230.097

sources.claim: The Fremont Bridge Bicycle Counter began operation in October 2012 and records bicycles crossing the bridge on the pedestrian and bicycle pathways. Inductive loops on the east and west pathways count the passing of bicycles REGARDLESS of travel direction. The data consists of a date and time field plus east and west pathway count fields giving the total bicycles detected in each one-hour period, published on the City of Seattle Open Data portal.
sources.citation: City of Seattle Open Data portal, Fremont Bridge Bicycle Counter

rejectedClaims.claim: The Fremont Bridge counter has documented outages that read as zeros, so missing data looks like a collapse in cycling.
rejectedClaims.why: Plausible and pedagogically attractive, but the dataset documentation reviewed did not confirm any specific outage or gap history, so it is not asserted on the page. The two traps that ARE taught (single-sensor sampling, and pathway columns not being directions) are both stated in the city's own dataset description.

rejectedClaims.claim: A specific Indian American population figure for Washington State.
rejectedClaims.why: Not verified at a source we were willing to cite, so no number appears on the page. The page names the tech-corridor cities instead, which is what the audience recognises anyway.

coding-classes-in-virginia.curriculumAuthority: 2017 Computer Science Standards of Learning, adopted November 2017, taught from 2019-20. Virginia was the FIRST state to require computer science instruction at all K-12 levels. K-8 is addressed WITHIN existing content areas; middle and high school are stand-alone electives. The page's spine is that integration is the most fragile delivery model: no timetable slot, no specialist teacher, no assessment to reveal absence.
coding-classes-in-virginia.localProject: Virginia School Quality Profiles / VDOE SOL pass rates, published for schools, divisions and the state across three years. Trap: REGRESSION TO THE MEAN. Select the bottom tenth of schools in year one and they rise in year two with no intervention, because selecting on an extreme selects partly for bad luck and luck does not repeat. Mirror it with the top tenth falling. Consequence: any programme aimed at the worst performers appears to work even if it does nothing, so an evaluation without a comparison group is worthless. Seventh distinct KIND of error in the cluster. Framed explicitly as being about statistics, not about judging schools.
requiredMentions: critical thinking, creative thinking, collaboration, communication, and citizenship

sources.claim: In November 2017 Virginia became the first state to require computer science instruction integrated at all K-12 levels, adopting K-12 Computer Science Standards of Learning, expected to be taught from the 2019-2020 academic year. Computer science in grades K-8 is addressed within the content areas, including language arts and history, while middle and high school classes are designed as stand-alone electives.
sources.citation: Virginia Department of Education, 2017 Computer Science Standards of Learning

sources.claim: A Standard Diploma requires at least 22 standard credits and 5 verified credits. An Advanced Studies Diploma requires at least 26 standard credits and 5 verified credits. Standard credits are earned by completing required and elective courses; verified credits are earned by completing required courses AND passing associated end-of-course SOL tests or other Board-approved assessments.
sources.citation: Virginia Department of Education, Standard and Advanced Studies Diploma graduation requirements

sources.claim: In accordance with the Profile of a Virginia Graduate, students shall acquire and demonstrate foundational skills in Virginia's 5 C's: critical thinking, creative thinking, collaboration, communication, and citizenship.
sources.citation: Virginia Department of Education, Profile of a Virginia Graduate

sources.claim: The Virginia Department of Education publishes School Quality Profiles containing accreditation, historical Standards of Learning scores and passing rates, and provides downloadable SOL test results for schools, school divisions and the state by grade level, course and content area covering three years with numerators and denominators.
sources.citation: Virginia Department of Education, SOL Test Pass Rates and Other Results; Virginia School Quality Profiles

sources.claim: Virginia has 157,635 Indian Americans, 1.83 percent of the state population.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

rejectedClaims.claim: Because Virginia requires computer science K-12, every Virginia child is learning to code.
rejectedClaims.why: The requirement is real and Virginia genuinely got there first, but K-8 delivery is integration into other subjects with no dedicated lesson, teacher or assessment. The page credits the policy, states the delivery model plainly, says explicitly that integration done well is genuinely good and that the problem is variance rather than ceiling, and gives parents a specific question to ask their own school instead of asserting a failure we cannot measure.

coding-classes-in-illinois.curriculumAuthority: Illinois computer science learning standards, written by the State Board of Education under HB 2170 and delivered by the end of 2021. The legal frame is an ENTITLEMENT to be offered a course, which is the page's spine: a floor, not a ceiling.
coding-classes-in-illinois.localProject: Chicago Data Portal beach water quality. Chicago Park District issues a swim advisory when predicted E. coli reaches at least 235 Colony Forming Units per 100 ml, and publishes lab data, advisories and model predictions daily through the season. Trap: CLASS IMBALANCE and the accuracy paradox. Advisories are rare, so a model that always answers safe scores about the same accuracy as a real one. Forces confusion matrix, precision and recall, and the judgement that a missed advisory and a false alarm are not equivalent harms. Sixth distinct KIND of error in the cluster.

sources.claim: HB 2170, the Education and Workforce Equity Act, was signed in March 2021 and championed by the Illinois Legislative Black Caucus. It requires schools to offer every student the opportunity to take at least one computer science course aligned to rigorous CS learning standards beginning in the 2023-2024 school year; requires ISBE to develop computer science learning standards, delivered by the end of 2021; requires districts to ensure students gain computer literacy skills starting in elementary school; and requires high school students to take one year of a course that includes intensive instruction in computer literacy beginning in the 2022-2023 school year.
sources.citation: Illinois HB 2170, Education and Workforce Equity Act, 2021

sources.claim: Chicago Public Schools made computer science a high school graduation requirement in 2016, ahead of the state and ahead of almost every large district in the United States.
sources.citation: Contemporaneous reporting on the CPS graduation requirement, 2016

sources.claim: The Chicago Park District monitors Lake Michigan beach water quality, testing for Escherichia coli as an indicator species, and a swim advisory is issued when the predicted E. coli level is at least 235 Colony Forming Units per 100 ml. The Chicago Data Portal publishes Beach E. coli Predictions, Beach Lab Data and Beach Swim Advisories, updated daily during the beach season. The City worked with the Park District, volunteer data scientists and university students on the forecasting model.
sources.citation: City of Chicago Data Portal, Beach E. coli Predictions

sources.claim: Illinois has 260,055 Indian Americans, 2.03 percent of the state population.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

rejectedClaims.claim: An AP computer science course counts toward the three years of mathematics required for graduation in Illinois.
rejectedClaims.why: Widely reported but not confirmed at primary source, and the New Jersey lesson applies: a credential claim that resists sourcing gets stated as unconfirmed, never asserted. The page and its FAQ say plainly that we could not confirm it and direct families to their counsellor for the rule in force for their cohort.

coding-classes-in-new-york.curriculumAuthority: New York State Learning Standards for Computer Science and Digital Fluency, adopted by the Board of Regents in December 2020, full implementation expected by September 2024. Five concept areas, grade bands K-1, 2-3, 4-6, 7-8, 9-12. Distinctive because Cybersecurity is named as a top-level concept, which very few states do.
coding-classes-in-new-york.localProject: NYC Open Data 311 Service Requests, over 40 million rows by end of 2025, updated daily. Trap: rate versus count, the denominator problem. Ranking boroughs by raw noise complaints mostly ranks them by population. Second layer: a 311 record measures somebody choosing to report, not the event itself. Deliberately a fifth distinct KIND of error, and specifically NOT Texas's observation bias, which was about detection changing over time; this is about comparing groups of different sizes at one moment.

sources.claim: The Board of Regents adopted the New York State Learning Standards for Computer Science and Digital Fluency in December 2020, following a two-year statewide collaborative authoring, reviewing and revision process. Five concept areas: Impacts of Computing, Computational Thinking, Networks and System Design, Cybersecurity, and Digital Literacy. Standards are grouped into grade bands K-1, 2-3, 4-6, 7-8 and 9-12. All K-12 schools were expected to fully implement by September 2024.
sources.citation: New York State Education Department, Computer Science and Digital Fluency Learning Standards

sources.claim: On 4 November 2024 the State Education Department presented NY Inspires, implementing the Blue Ribbon Commission on Graduation Measures recommendations through four transformations: adopt the New York State Portrait of a Graduate, redefine credits, sunset diploma assessment requirements, and move to one diploma. Until specific changes are approved by the Board of Regents, current graduation requirements remain in effect for all public school students. Reporting has indicated the Regents exam requirement ending around the 2027-28 school year.
sources.citation: New York State Education Department, Current Diploma Requirements and the Graduation Measures Initiative

sources.claim: NYC Open Data publishes 311 Service Requests covering 2010 to the present, updated daily, split into a 2010-2019 historical set and a 2020-to-present set. As of December 2025 the data contained over 40 million rows. Each row includes complaint type, responding agency and geographic location.
sources.citation: NYC Open Data, 311 Service Requests

sources.claim: New York has 387,376 Indian Americans, 1.92 percent of the state population.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

sources.claim: The Hecht-Calandra Act of 1971 requires New York City to admit students to its specialized high schools solely on performance in the Specialized High Schools Admissions Test. The legislation originally covered Stuyvesant High School, the Bronx High School of Science and Brooklyn Technical High School. The SHSAT is the sole criterion for eight of the nine specialized high schools; the ninth, LaGuardia, admits by audition or portfolio.
sources.citation: New York Education Law, Hecht-Calandra Act 1971; NYC specialized high schools admissions

rejectedClaims.claim: New York students no longer need to pass Regents exams to graduate.
rejectedClaims.why: Premature. The direction is announced and the plan is published, but until the Board of Regents approves specific changes the current requirements remain in force for every public school student. The page states the plan, states plainly that nothing has changed yet, and tells families to confirm the position for their child's cohort with the school.

coding-classes-in-california.curriculumAuthority: California Computer Science Standards, adopted by the State Board of Education on 6 September 2018. Six core concepts and seven core practices, aligned to the K-12 Computer Science Framework. Crucially VOLUNTARY, which is the page's central fact and the sharpest contrast with New Jersey and Texas.
coding-classes-in-california.localProject: CAL FIRE incident acreage. Trap: heavy-tailed distribution defeating a summary statistic. In 2020 nearly 10,000 fires burned over 4.2 million acres, a mean near 400 acres per fire, but the August Complex alone exceeded one million acres, close to a quarter of the season, while most fires were tiny. The mean describes no actual fire and no arithmetic error exists anywhere. Comparing mean acreage across years mostly measures whether a megafire happened. Deliberately a fourth distinct KIND of error: New Jersey metric definition, Ontario model misspecification, Texas observation bias, California summary statistics on a heavy tail.
requiredMentions: six core concepts and seven core practices

sources.claim: The State Board of Education adopted California's first K-12 computer science standards on 6 September 2018. They are built on six core computer science concepts and seven core practices, aligned to the K-12 Computer Science Framework, and developed with input from CSTA, NSF-funded work and industry. They are voluntary, intended to give substantive guidance while allowing flexibility across local education agencies to decide how best to incorporate computer science based on local capacity and context.
sources.citation: California Department of Education, Computer Science Content Standards

sources.claim: UC subject requirement Area D asks for two years of laboratory science providing fundamental knowledge in at least two of biology, chemistry and physics, with a third year recommended. Computer science, engineering and applied science courses can be used in Area D as an additional science, that is a third year and beyond, not toward the core two years. Area G is one year of college-preparatory elective. Courses must be approved by UC and appear on the school's a-g course list.
sources.citation: University of California, A-G subject requirements, Subject Area D: Science

sources.claim: In the 2020 California fire season nearly 10,000 fires burned over 4.2 million acres, the largest wildfire season in California's modern recorded history. The August Complex exceeded one million acres, described as the first gigafire, formed from around 30 separate lightning-caused fires in the Mendocino National Forest that converged.
sources.citation: CAL FIRE 2020 incident archive; contemporaneous reporting on the 2020 fire siege

sources.claim: California has 830,259 Indian Americans, 2.1 percent of the state population, the largest such population of any US state in absolute terms.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

rejectedClaims.claim: Computer science counts as a laboratory science for University of California admission.
rejectedClaims.why: Half true and therefore dangerous. It counts only as an ADDITIONAL science, third year and beyond, and does not replace the required two years drawn from biology, chemistry and physics. A student who plans as though it substitutes arrives in Grade 12 short. The page states the distinction explicitly and contrasts it with the Texas LOTE rule, which genuinely is a substitution.

coding-classes-in-texas.curriculumAuthority: Technology Applications TEKS, revised by the State Board of Education in 2022, implemented from the 2024-25 school year. Five strands, with computational thinking the largest departure from the 2011 standards.
coding-classes-in-texas.localProject: NOAA Storm Prediction Center tornado records for Texas. Trap: observation bias. Reported counts climb since 1950, but population spread, the 1990s Doppler radar rollout and the 2007 switch from the Fujita to the Enhanced Fujita scale all changed detection. NOAA's own assessment is that removing F/EF0 counts nearly eliminates the annual frequency trend. Method taught: find a subset whose collection method did not change (strong tornadoes) and see whether the trend survives. Deliberately a different KIND of error from New Jersey (metric definition) and Ontario (model misspecification).
requiredMentions: Computer Science I, II and III

sources.claim: 19 TAC 74.12 Languages Other Than English, two credits: 'The credits may be selected from the following: (i) any two levels in the same language, including comparable AP or IB language courses that do not count toward another credit required for graduation; or (ii) two credits in computer programming languages, including computer coding, to be selected from Computer Science I, II, and III, AP Computer Science Principles, AP Computer Science A, IB Computer Science Standard Level, and IB Computer Science Higher Level.' A separate provision covers a student who cannot complete a second LOTE credit, requiring agreement from the LOTE teacher, the principal or designee and the parent, or the ARD committee, or the Section 504 committee. NOTE the copy consulted is marked effective until 2025-08-01 and TEA issued an August 2025 update to Chapter 74 Subchapter B; the page tells families to confirm the current text.
sources.citation: 19 Tex. Admin. Code section 74.12, Foundation High School Program

sources.claim: Technology Applications TEKS were revised in 2022 and implemented from the 2024-25 school year. Five strands: computational thinking; creativity and innovation; data literacy, management, and representation; digital citizenship; and practical technology concepts. Computational thinking breaks problem solving into decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithms. The 2022 revision gave each grade K to 5 its own standards instead of grade bands.
sources.citation: Texas Education Agency, Technology Applications; SBOE April 2022 adoption

sources.claim: The Foundation High School Program requires at least 22 credits; an endorsement takes the total to 26. Subject minimums include English 4, Mathematics 3, Science 3, Social Studies 3, Languages Other Than English 2, Physical Education 1, Fine Arts 1 and Electives 5. Endorsement options are STEM, business and industry, public services, arts and humanities, and multidisciplinary studies. The Distinguished Level of Achievement requires 26 credits including Algebra II.
sources.citation: Texas Education Agency, Graduation Toolkit 2025

sources.claim: Inconsistencies in the NOAA severe events database arise from changes in population awareness, reporting practices, Doppler radar technology and NWS guidelines, which have likely introduced artificial trends. Removing F/EF0 counts from the database nearly eliminates the annual frequency trend. The 2007 change from the Fujita to the Enhanced Fujita scale produced large increases in weak tornado reports.
sources.citation: NOAA State of the Science Fact Sheet: Tornadoes, Climate Variability and Climate Change, September 2023

sources.claim: Texas has 480,566 Indian Americans, 1.65 percent of the state population, the second largest such population of any US state.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

rejectedClaims.claim: A Texas student needs district or principal approval to use computer science for the LOTE requirement.
rejectedClaims.why: This confuses two separate provisions of 19 TAC 74.12. Clause (ii) is an unconditional listed alternative needing no permission. The named-approval process belongs to the different provision covering a student who has begun a language and is unlikely to complete the second credit. The page explains both and distinguishes them, because families are routinely quoted the wrong one.

coding-classes-in-ontario.curriculumAuthority: Ontario mathematics curriculum, Grades 1 to 8 (2020). Six strands, with coding placed inside the Algebra strand rather than taught as a separate subject. Ontario was the first province in Canada to do this.
coding-classes-in-ontario.localProject: IESO hourly Ontario electricity demand against temperature. Trap: the relationship is V-shaped, because Ontario heats in winter and cools in summer. A single straight-line fit returns a near-zero correlation and invites the student to conclude that temperature does not drive electricity demand, which is spectacularly wrong. The fix is to model two regimes, or to use heating and cooling degree days. This is a model-misspecification trap, deliberately a different KIND of error from the metric-definition trap used on the New Jersey page.
requiredMentions: Social-Emotional Learning Skills and Mathematical Processes
Digital Technology and Innovations in the Changing World

sources.claim: The 2020 Ontario Grades 1 to 8 mathematics curriculum has six strands: Number, Algebra, Data, Spatial Sense, Financial Literacy, and Social-Emotional Learning Skills and Mathematical Processes. Coding sits inside the Algebra strand. Grade 1 students write code to order a sequence of steps; Grade 2 develop code to move multiple objects from one location on a grid to another; Grade 3 write code to perform a repeating operation such as a repeating add 3; Grade 4 write and read code to create geometric designs.
sources.citation: Government of Ontario, mathematics curriculum Grades 1 to 8, effective 2020

sources.claim: OSSD requires a minimum of 30 credits. Students entering Grade 9 in 2023 or earlier need 18 compulsory and 12 optional; those entering in 2024-25 onwards need 17 compulsory and 13 optional. All cohorts must earn at least two of the 30 credits online. Students must meet the literacy graduation requirement via the OSSLT, the OSSLC, or an adjudication process, and complete 40 hours of community involvement activities.
sources.citation: Ontario Schools, Kindergarten to Grade 12: Policy and Program Requirements, section 6

sources.claim: Starting in the 2026-2027 school year, students who enter Grade 9 in 2025-2026 and onwards must meet a Financial Literacy Graduation Requirement, achieving a mark of 70 percent or higher on the financial literacy modules.
sources.citation: Ontario Schools, Kindergarten to Grade 12: Policy and Program Requirements, section 6

sources.claim: The IESO Data Directory publishes Ontario demand and market demand for each hour, plus hourly electricity consumption aggregated by Forward Sortation Area, which is the first three characters of a postal code. It also publishes the Hourly Ontario Energy Price.
sources.citation: Independent Electricity System Operator, Data Directory

sources.claim: Ontario secondary computer studies runs on The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 10 to 12: Computer Studies, revised 2008. Course codes: ICS3U (Grade 11 university preparation), ICS3C (Grade 11 college preparation), ICS4U (Grade 12 university preparation), ICS4C (Grade 12 college preparation). The Grade 10 course ICS2O was replaced from September 2023 by ICD2O, Digital Technology and Innovations in the Changing World. ICS3U and ICS4U remain on the 2008 revision.
sources.citation: Ontario Ministry of Education, The Ontario Curriculum Grades 10 to 12: Computer Studies, 2008 Revised

sources.claim: Ontario has 1,052,045 residents of Indian origin, 7.5 percent of the provincial population, the largest such population of any Canadian province.
sources.citation: 2021 Census of Canada

rejectedClaims.claim: Our courses can count toward the two online credits the OSSD requires.
rejectedClaims.why: We are not an Ontario Ministry of Education inspected private school and cannot grant OSSD credits. The page states this plainly rather than implying otherwise, because a family could otherwise plan a graduation pathway around us and be badly wrong.

coding-classes-in-new-jersey.curriculumAuthority: New Jersey Student Learning Standards for Computer Science and Design Thinking (NJSLS-CSDT), adopted 2020, K to 12
coding-classes-in-new-jersey.localProject: NJ Transit punctuality. Trap: cancellations are reported as a separate statistic and sit outside On-Time Performance entirely, so a line that cancels services can post better punctuality than one that runs everything late. Second trap: two rail dashboards exist for the same trains, all-causes and Amtrak-adjusted.

sources.claim: Every public school enrolling grades 9 to 12, other than a county vocational school district, must offer a computer science course from the 2018 to 2019 school year, covering computational thinking, computer programming, appropriate use of the internet and development of internet web pages, data security and prevention of data breaches, ethical matters, and global impact.
sources.citation: N.J.S.A. 18A:7C-1.1, P.L. 2017 c.303, enacted 16 January 2018

sources.claim: New Jersey state minimum graduation requirements total 120 credits. Mathematics 15 credits including Algebra I, Geometry and a third year building on them. Science 15 credits with at least 5 in laboratory biology or life science. Technology is integrated throughout all courses rather than a separate credit line. There is no computer science credit line in the state minimum.
sources.citation: N.J.A.C. 6A:8-5.1, New Jersey State Minimum Graduation Requirements by Content Area

sources.claim: NJSLS-CSDT covers Kindergarten through grade 12. Computer science concepts: Computing Systems; Networks and the Internet; Impacts of Computing; Data and Analysis; Algorithms and Programming. Design thinking concepts: Engineering Design; Interaction of Technology and Humans; Nature of Technology; Effects of Technology on the Natural World; Ethics and Culture.
sources.citation: New Jersey Department of Education, Computer Science and Design Thinking standards page

sources.claim: NJ Transit publishes On-Time Performance, Mean Distance Between Failure and Total Cancellations. A vehicle operating within 6 minutes of published schedule counts as on time. Two rail dashboards exist: All Causes, and Adjusted for Amtrak-related Causes.
sources.citation: NJ Transit performance dashboards

sources.claim: New Jersey has 415,342 Indian Americans, 4.47 percent of the state population, the highest concentration of any US state.
sources.citation: 2020 United States Census

rejectedClaims.claim: An Advanced Placement computer science course satisfies part of the New Jersey mathematics credit requirement for graduation.
rejectedClaims.why: Could not be confirmed at primary source. Absent from the state minimum graduation requirements chart at N.J.A.C. 6A:8-5.1 and from the Cornell LII text of that regulation. Second-hand accounts conflict on the starting grade nine class year (2014-2015 vs 2016-2017) and on whether it covers mathematics only or mathematics or science. Page now states it as unconfirmed and directs families to their school counsellor.

coding-classes-in-oman.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. Grade 11 is internally assessed; Grade 12 is sat as external Ministry examinations. Eight subjects, five compulsory and three optional, and a student must pass all eight. The page's argument is that a system with no droppable subject leaves no slack, so the weekly cost of a class has to be stated honestly.

sources.claim: Oman's Governorates System lists the three wilayats of Al Buraimi, Mahdha and As-Sunaynah, and names the Wilayat of Al Buraimi as the governorate centre.
The governorate was established through Royal Decree 108/2006, lies in northwestern Oman and is described as a crossroads for trade routes in the southeastern Arabian Peninsula.
The government portal lists separate wali leadership for the three wilayats and Sunday-through-Thursday office hours.
The official Mahdah page identifies it as the largest of the governorate's wilayats and describes a mountain chain separating it from the North Al Batinah wilayats.

The Wilayat Al Buraimi page describes its forts, towers, traditional markets and historic houses, the most prominent being Al-Khandaq Fort and Al-Hilla Fort, and reports a wilayat population of about 118,076 for January 2024.

Al-Buraimi is an oasis city and wilayah in northern Oman on the border with the UAE and the capital of Al Buraimi Governorate, roughly 343 km from Muscat, forming part of the historical region of Tawam or Al-Buraimi Oasis, with Al Ain the adjacent city on the UAE side.

rejectedClaims: A single population for the wilayat. About 118,076 is reported for January 2024 and the 2020 census gives 110,171; the dates differ so both appear with their dates and neither is adopted as the figure.
A construction date for either fort. Al Khandaq is dated to the 19th century, which is a band rather than a year, and Al Hillah is described as likely built to succeed it. Both hedges are kept.
A combined figure for the Al Buraimi and Al Ain sides of the oasis. The two lie under different states with different statistical systems, and no cross-border total is offered.

A separate page for the wilayat. This page's own H1 already reads Coding classes in Al Buraimi and ranks for that query, so the wilayat is served by deepening this page rather than by a second one competing with it.

coding-classes-in-netherlands.curriculumAuthority: Dutch digital literacy core objectives. Until this reform there was NO compulsory education in digital literacy or informatics in Dutch primary or lower secondary schooling. In 2022 the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science tasked SLO (Netherlands Institute for Curriculum Development) with developing core objectives; the curriculum was FINALISED IN MARCH 2024 with nine core objectives in three domains: (A) practical knowledge and skills, (B) designing and making, (C) interaction between digital technology, media, people and society. Digital literacy is defined as ICT skills + media literacy + information literacy + computational thinking, with CT integrated throughout. The page argument: a finalised curriculum is a starting gun, not a description of classrooms, so the honest answer to what a child already covers is school-dependent and parents should ask. Deliberate CONTRAST with the Hong Kong page, where a published hours figure exists.
coding-classes-in-netherlands.localProject: A policy date is not an outcome date. Core objectives finalised March 2024; a 2026 primary leaver spent most of their schooling before that, so the policy cannot have caused most of what a 2026 measurement records. Distinct from a plain correlation-causation exercise: both facts are real and in the right order, the flaw is EXPOSURE. Unused across all 46 existing pages.

coding-classes-in-maryland.curriculumAuthority: Blueprint for Maryland's Future, College and Career Readiness standard. Students are expected to meet the CCR standard BY THE END OF TENTH GRADE, with reevaluation in eleventh and twelfth. Three route groups: Option 1 academic benchmarks (cumulative unweighted GPA 3.0 at end of 10th or 11th AND a final grade of A/B/C in Algebra 1 or Performance Level 3/4 on Algebra 1 MCAP); Option 2 standardized test benchmarks (Level 3/4 on ELA 10 MCAP AND a qualifying Algebra MCAP level or SAT math 520 minimum); Option 3 career connected benchmarks from 2025-2026, nine further measures incl. two dual enrollment courses, AP 3+, IB 4+, ACT WorkKeys Silver+, industry credentials, registered apprenticeships, ASVAB 50+. Just over 50 per cent met the standard at the end of 2024-25. DELIBERATELY NOT the 'state CS standards adopted in year X' axis, which all nine existing US and Canadian pages already use. The argument is TIMING: the decisive checkpoint is two years earlier than most states, so middle school and ninth grade are the years that matter, and Algebra 1 is load-bearing in more than one route.
coding-classes-in-maryland.localProject: An OR across many tests is not one measurement. A learner writes a CCR checker that returns true if ANY route is satisfied, then proves in their own output that adding a clause to an OR can only ever grow the pass set, never shrink it. So a rising readiness rate cannot distinguish students improving from a door being added, and MSDE analysis documents that adding the HSGPA route INCREASED the percentage meeting the standard. The fix is to publish the rate with the definition and the date it last changed, then re-run the old definition on the new data. Checked against all 47 built pages; unused.

coding-classes-in-british-columbia.curriculumAuthority: BC Applied Design, Skills and Technologies (ADST), quoted from the Ministry introduction. coding-classes-in-british-columbia.localProject: Combinations versus permutations. Asked how many different module years are possible, learners compute 8x7x6=336, which counts ORDERED selections and overcounts every set of three by 6. The answer is 56. They then generalise to dividing by k factorial and verify the formula against a brute-force enumeration for small n. Checked against all 48 built pages; unused.

coding-classes-in-alberta.curriculumAuthority: Alberta CTS Computing Science (CSE), verified from the Calgary Board of Education CBe-learn listing. Every course is worth 1 CREDIT, students usually aim to complete five in a semester, and an Alberta High School Diploma requires a minimum of 100 credits, so one CSE course is one per cent of a diploma and competes with fine arts, second languages and PE for the same optional space. The load-bearing structure is the PREREQUISITE GRAPH: CSE1110 Structured Programming 1 (none) -> CSE1120 (needs 1110) -> CSE2110 Procedural Programming 1 (needs 1120) -> CSE2120 Data Structures 1 (needs 2110) -> CSE3110 Iterative Algorithm 1 (needs 2120) -> CSE3310 Recursive Algorithms 1 (needs 3110 AND 3120), with CSE3120 Object-oriented Programming 1 needing 2110. Client-side Scripting 1 and 2 and the CSE project courses have NO prerequisite. Argument: six links deep and high school is six semesters, so the ORDER decides whether the deep end is reachable, and arriving at Grade 10 already able to program is worth a semester. Deliberately different from BC (rotations, no credit) and Ontario (coding inside compulsory Algebra strand).
coding-classes-in-alberta.localProject: Longest path through a dependency graph, i.e. capacity does not beat dependency. Six courses at five per semester looks like two semesters; the bound is the DEPTH of the chain, six, because a queue is not shortened by spare capacity. The learner builds the graph as course-to-prerequisites, writes a longest-chain function, and finds adding capacity changes nothing while removing one prerequisite changes everything. Critical path as a real algorithm rather than a metaphor. Checked against all 49 built pages; unused.

coding-classes-in-brunei.curriculumAuthority: SPN21, Brunei's National Education System for the 21st Century, administered by the Ministry of Education. Primary runs Year 1 to Year 6 ending in the Penilaian Sekolah Rendah (Primary School Assessment). Secondary runs Year 7 to Year 11: Years 7 and 8 are lower secondary ending in the Student Progress Assessment, and Years 9 to 11 are upper secondary ending in the Brunei-Cambridge GCE Ordinary Level, a qualification jointly branded with Cambridge rather than a purely national one. A learner may opt for a shorter two years of upper secondary instead of three, subject to evaluation of their lower secondary academic record. The Ministry administered or oversaw 232 schools across preschool, primary and secondary as of 2019, in a country of 458,604 people. THE SPINE OF THIS PAGE IS NOT THE CURRICULUM, it is the calendar: Ministry of Finance and Economy division listings state working days as Monday to Thursday and Saturday, Friday varies by division and Sunday appears on none of them, so Saturday is a working day and Brunei is widely described as the only country with a non-contiguous working week. Much of the private sector runs Monday to Friday instead, so two Bruneian households can have completely different free days. The page therefore refuses to publish a default weekly slot. Deliberately NOT led on: the express two-year upper secondary route, which is real and verified but is structurally the same 'the decisive moment is earlier than you think' argument as the Kuwait and Maryland pages, so it sits in the SPN21 section rather than the spine.
coding-classes-in-brunei.localProject: The weekend is an input, not a constant. The learner writes the working-days-between-two-dates function every programmer has written, tests it, passes, then runs it for a family in Brunei and is wrong by roughly a day a week, compounding, with no error raised. Every mainstream date library, spreadsheet function and tutorial hardcodes Saturday and Sunday, usually not even as a parameter. The fix reframes the function: the set of non-working days stops being a constant inside the code and becomes an argument passed in, which forces the caller to know it, which forces somebody to ask. In Brunei asking is unavoidable because the answer differs between a government household and an oil-sector one, so one program yields two correct answers depending on an input the original version did not have. Distinct from every other page in the cluster: this is a genuine hardcoded-locale bug rather than a statistical misreading, and it is the only page whose trap the market's own calendar creates. Unused across all 52 existing pages.

two and a half hours ahead

coding-classes-in-bandar-seri-begawan.curriculumAuthority: SPN21 under Brunei's Ministry of Education, the same system as the country page, so this page deliberately does NOT re-argue the curriculum. Its subject is the administrative shape of the capital. Bandar Seri Begawan sits in Brunei-Muara, the smallest and most populous of the four districts at 332,462 residents. The municipality is estimated at 72,133 people and is composed of THIRTEEN mukims: Berakas 'A', Berakas 'B', Burong Pingai Ayer, Gadong 'A', Gadong 'B', Kianggeh, Kilanas, Kota Batu, Peramu, Saba, Sungai Kebun, Sungai Kedayan and Tamoi. SIX of those thirteen are Kampong Ayer, the stilt settlement over the Brunei River, and both mukim lists were cross-checked so the subset relation is exact. Awang Semaun Secondary School is described as the only school of its kind whose buildings are built on water. On 1 August 2007 the municipal area went from 12.87 to 100.36 square kilometres, roughly eight times larger, with nobody moving house, which is used ONLY as a practical travel-time point because 'the boundary is part of the statistic' is the Birmingham page's argument and must not be repeated here.
coding-classes-in-bandar-seri-begawan.localProject: You cannot add a part to its whole. The learner is asked how many people live in the capital and its water village, given 72,133 for the city and 10,250 for Kampong Ayer at the 2016 census, and almost everybody adds them to 82,383. But Kampong Ayer's six mukims are six of the capital's thirteen, so the smaller set is entirely contained in the larger, the intersection IS the smaller set, and the union collapses to 72,133. The addition overstated by exactly 10,250, which is 14.2 per cent. The rule taken away: before adding two counts, name one person who is in the first and not the second; if you cannot describe that person the sets are nested and addition is a category error whose size depends on the overlap rather than on the magnitude of the numbers. The extension turns the same discipline on the two census columns: the total falls 10,250 to 8,902 between 2016 and 2021, about 13 per cent, yet two of the six mukims RISE (Peramu 1,111 to 1,151, Sungai Kedayan 230 to 241), so a direction true of a total can be false of its parts. Every mukim figure was fetched from that mukim's own record and the 2016 column sums exactly to the reported 10,250. Distinct from every other page: this is set membership, not a boundary definition and not a statistical misreading.
requiredMentions: You cannot add a part to its whole

Kampong Ayer comprises six mukims (Burong Pingai Ayer, Peramu, Saba, Sungai Kebun, Sungai Kedayan, Tamoi), its 2016 census population was 10,250, the settlement held about 28,000 people in 1981 and about 13,000 in 2011, and Awang Semaun Secondary School is the only school of its kind with buildings built on water.

coding-classes-in-kuala-belait.curriculumAuthority: TWO curricula in one district, which is what makes Belait unlike anywhere else in Brunei. The load-bearing consequence for a parent: every Panaga pupil changes school at thirteen, to Jerudong, to a government secondary school, or to another country, which is the reason to have built something by twelve rather than to be busier at fourteen. Belait carries five secondary and sixteen primary public schools. That failure is loud and harmless. The QUIET version is in the same dataset: sorted largest to smallest as text, the largest place in Belait is reported as Sukang with 81 residents, then Labi, then Bukit Sawat, then Melilas with 29, and only then Kuala Belait with 28,793. The check that catches both: the parts must reconcile with the published total, and 28,793 + 18,313 + 16,813 + 759 + 727 + 81 + 29 + 16 is exactly 65,531. coding-classes-in-tutong.curriculumAuthority: SPN21 under Brunei's Ministry of Education, the same national system as the country page, so this page does not re-argue the curriculum ladder. Its subject is SUPPLY. Tutong covers 1,166 sq km and recorded 47,210 residents at the 2021 census across eight mukims, the largest being Telisai at 13,253 and the smallest Rambai at 980. A viable class needs five to eight learners sharing a level, a subject and a free hour, and those conditions multiply rather than add, so in a pool this size the set that clears all four is frequently empty. The district's one specialist institution is TUTONG SIXTH FORM CENTRE, which teaches A Level alongside secondary schools including Muda Hashim, Raja Isteri Pengiran Anak Saleha, Sayyidina 'Othman, Sufri Bolkiah and Tanjong Maya. That gives the page its timing argument, distinct from the other Brunei pages: sixth form is where a subject becomes a specialism, so a learner should arrive there having already built things rather than spend the first of two years catching up. Geography used as texture, not as argument: the 137 km Tutong River, Bukit Bedawan at 529 m, and Tasek Merimbun, Brunei's largest natural lake, an ASEAN Heritage Park since 29 November 1984. Population is Tutong, Dusun, Kedayan, Iban and Chinese.
coding-classes-in-tutong.localProject: The midrange is not the median. Asked how big a typical Tutong mukim is, a learner takes the halfway point between Telisai's 13,253 and Rambai's 980 and gets 7,116.5, which is one keystroke in a spreadsheet and feels like the middle. FIVE of the eight mukims are below it; only Telisai, Pekan Tutong and Keriam are above. The two statistics that use all the data give 5,901.25 (mean) and 4,417.5 (median), so three defensible answers spread across 2,699, which is more than the entire population of Ukong and nearly three times Rambai's. The demonstration that makes it stick: delete the largest and smallest values and the midrange moves to 5,956 while the median stays at EXACTLY 4,417.5, because the midrange is computed from the two extremes and the median is computed from everything except them. The midrange is not a statistic that happens to be sensitive to outliers, it is a statistic made of nothing but outliers. Every figure verified in python before writing, and the eight mukims sum to exactly the published 47,210. Distinct from the other pages in the cluster: Bandar Seri Begawan is set membership, Kuala Belait is data type, this one is choice of summary statistic.

coding-classes-in-temburong.curriculumAuthority: SPN21 under Brunei's Ministry of Education, argued in full on the country page and not repeated here. This page's subject is SUPPLY OF ONE. Temburong is an exclave divided from the rest of Brunei by the Malaysian district of Limbang. It covers 1,306 sq km, the second largest district, and recorded 9,444 residents at the 2021 census, up from 8,852 in 2011 and estimated at about 9,600 by 2024. Bangar is the district town. It has thirteen primary schools, public and private, and exactly ONE secondary school, Sultan Hassan Secondary School, so for a specialised subject a learner is choosing between the one thing that exists and nothing. Ulu Temburong National Park covers more than 500 sq km with a canopy walkway at 250 metres; the Peradayan, Selirong and Labu forest reserves hold mangrove and old growth. The Sultan Haji Omar Ali Saifuddien Bridge opened in 2020 and cut the road journey to the capital from two or more hours via Sarawak, requiring four international passport checks, to about thirty minutes. The page's commercial argument turns on that precisely: the bridge fixed transport and nothing else, and what 9,444 people cannot supply is not travel but a room of five to eight learners at the same level.
coding-classes-in-temburong.localProject: The network changed, not the map. A learner writes a travel-time program from coordinates and straight-line distance, which passes on a dozen town pairs, then runs it on Bangar and Bandar Seri Begawan for 2019 and for 2021. It returns the SAME number for both years and was wrong in both: too optimistic in 2019, when the only road route crossed another country and four checkpoints, and too pessimistic in 2021, after the bridge. Nothing on the map moved between those dates, so a coordinate model cannot see the difference and never signals difficulty. The rewrite is a graph: places as nodes, connections as edges, edge cost including the border checks. Bangar and the capital were always close; before 2020 they were simply not adjacent. Distance is a property of geometry, cost is a property of the network, and a model built on the wrong quantity produces stable, plausible answers for years and fails silently on the day the network changes, which is the day somebody is relying on it. Distinct from every other page in the cluster: Bandar Seri Begawan is set membership, Kuala Belait is data type, Tutong is choice of summary statistic, this one is choice of MODEL.
requiredMentions: Sultan Haji Omar Ali Saifuddien Bridge
The network changed, not the map
Distance is a property of geometry

coding-classes-in-seria.curriculumAuthority: SPN21 under Brunei's Ministry of Education, argued in full on the country page and the Kuala Belait page, not repeated here. This page's subject is SCALE MISMATCH plus SCHEDULE. Seria town recorded 2,659 residents at the 2021 census while Mukim Seria recorded 18,313, so the town is roughly a seventh of the mukim named after it and the two figures must be kept apart. The municipal area is 1.56 sq km and the town lies 65 km west of Bandar Seri Begawan. The field beneath it was located in 1929 by the British Malayan Petroleum Company, production began in 1931, first export 1932; by 1935 royalties were 47 per cent of state revenue and between 1932 and 1959 the government received $340 million in royalties; the field has been continuously in production since 1931. Around the town sit the Seria refinery (the only refinery in Brunei), the Seria Crude Oil Terminal, a gas compression plant, and at Panaga the headquarters of Brunei Shell Petroleum. The commercial argument is the SHIFT PATTERN: a town of 2,659 cannot fill a class at a given level, and its adults work rosters and rotations that a fixed local timetable does not survive, so the slot is agreed per household and pausing costs one month.
coding-classes-in-seria.localProject: A cumulative total can only go up. The Billionth Barrel Monument, built in 1991, marks the billionth barrel from a field producing since 1931; asked whether the field was doing well in 1991, most learners say yes. But a cumulative total is monotonic by construction, so its direction is fixed by arithmetic before any data arrives and carries no information. What the figure DOES support: 1931 to 1991 is sixty years, so an average of about 16.7 million barrels a year or roughly 45,600 a day, and a field producing ten times that in 1955 and a tenth of it in 1990 reaches the same total on the same date. The slope of the cumulative curve is the production rate, so a flattening curve describes decline and still points up and to the right. General rule: ask whether the quantity can move in both directions. Total users ever registered, total cases recorded, total revenue since founding: none can fall, so none can show that anything got worse. Arithmetic verified in python. Distinct from every other page in the cluster: Bandar Seri Begawan is set membership, Kuala Belait is data type, Tutong is choice of summary statistic, Temburong is choice of model, Gadong is choice of denominator, Liang is the join key, Jerudong is missing versus zero. This one is a quantity that is monotonic by construction.

coding-classes-in-liang.curriculumAuthority: SPN21 alongside the British-influenced international programme at Panaga, as set out on the Kuala Belait page and not re-argued here. This page's subject is GROWTH AND NAMES. Mukim Liang, in northern Belait on the South China Sea, recorded 14,301 residents at the 2016 census and 16,813 at the 2021 one, an increase of 2,512 or 17.6 per cent in five years, against the capital's six water village mukims falling from 10,250 to 8,902, about thirteen per cent, over the same interval. In 2016 the mukim was 32.3 per cent urban and 67.7 per cent rural and 51.4 per cent male. It contains twenty listed settlements and is anchored by the Sungai Liang Industrial Park with Brunei Fertilizer Industries. The commercial argument: provision follows population with a lag of years, so a growing young mukim is precisely where local options have not caught up, and an online group removes the wait entirely.
coding-classes-in-liang.localProject: Joining on a name merges things that are not the same. Three settlements in this mukim carry the name Lumut: Kampong Lumut with 171 residents, RPN Kampong Lumut Area 1 with 2,035 and RPN Kampong Lumut Area 2 with 5,605, together 7,811. A loose match collapses them into one row and reports the village at forty-five times its size; a strict match drops the two housing scheme rows and 7,640 people vanish with no error raised. One join, two opposite silent failures. The fix is not a better string comparison but to stop joining on names at all, because names get abbreviated, transliterated, prefixed with RPN, suffixed with Area 2 and renamed: an identifier is a value that exists in order to be matched and a name is not one. The check taught: count rows before and after the join; up means something matched more than once, down means something matched nothing. Distinct from Jerudong, which is about a lookup returning NOTHING, and from Gadong, which is about which population goes underneath a division.

coding-classes-in-gadong.curriculumAuthority: SPN21, with the Years 7 and 8 window and the Brunei-Cambridge GCE argued in full on the country and Bandar Seri Begawan pages. This page's subject is SCOPE. Kampong Gadong is a village and neighbourhood inside Bandar Seri Begawan, in Mukim Gadong 'B', covering 254.4872 hectares, and recorded 3,356 residents at the 2021 census. Mukim Gadong 'A' recorded 35,424 and Mukim Gadong 'B' 38,067, giving 73,491 between them. Brunei-Muara district recorded 318,530 and its eighteen mukims sum to EXACTLY that figure, which the page uses as its reconciliation check. Landmarks: the Centrepoint Hotel completed in 1994 as part of the Abdul Razak Complex, and The Mall with the Rizqun International Hotel inaugurated on 9 July 2006. IMPORTANT CONSISTENCY NOTE: 318,530 is the 2021 census figure for Brunei-Muara and the 332,462 used on the Bandar Seri Begawan page is a later estimate; the source note says so rather than letting the two sit unexplained.
coding-classes-in-gadong.localProject: The denominator is a choice, and a rate means nothing until you name it. Asked for shops per thousand people in Gadong, the learner finds four defensible populations: 3,356 for the village, 38,067 for the mukim containing it, 73,491 for both Gadong mukims, and 318,530 for the district whose residents actually shop there. The largest is ninety-five times the smallest, so the rate moves by that factor while the numerator never changes, and every one of the four is real and correctly cited. Nothing in the data selects between them, because rightness is a property of the question rather than of the numbers: how well served the residents are makes residents the denominator, how busy the shops are makes arrivals the denominator, and most of those live elsewhere. The discipline taught is to write the sentence before the code: this is X per Y, where Y is the population of, as of, counted by. General form: crime per resident in a district full of visitors, revenue per employee where half the staff are contractors, cases per capita where the population moved. Distinct from Bandar Seri Begawan's set membership, which asks whether one count sits INSIDE another; this asks which count belongs UNDERNEATH a division.

coding-classes-in-jerudong.curriculumAuthority: Several school systems in one area, which is why placement here is explicitly curriculum-independent; SPN21 itself is argued on the country page. This page's subject is a PLACE WITH NO ADMINISTRATIVE UNIT OF ITS OWN. There is NO Mukim Jerudong. Kampong Jerudong is a settlement of Mukim Sengkurong, which recorded 40,972 at the 2021 census and is the largest of Brunei-Muara's eighteen mukims. Kampong Jerudong itself recorded 3,856 at the 2016 census, covers 32.97 sq km, takes in twenty-three settlements and lies about 21 km from the capital. Institutions far larger than the resident population: Jerudong Park, opened 1994, free admission for years, revamped and relaunched 2014, amphitheatre concerts in 1996; Jerudong Park Medical Centre housing Gleneagles JPMC; The Empire, a five-star beach resort, opened 2000. Commercial argument: a small resident population wrapped around institutions that draw nationally, plus households that move, so nothing here depends on a building and a learner keeps the same teacher and group through a posting.
coding-classes-in-jerudong.localProject: An absent record is not a zero. A lookup for Jerudong in the mukim table returns nothing because the mukim is called Sengkurong, and what happens next is a choice usually made without noticing. A default of zero, or a fill after a merge, turns a fact the data does not contain into a fact it appears to assert: Jerudong, population 0. That row then enters the sum harmlessly, drags the mean down, wins the minimum, and sits at the bottom of the sorted table looking like a real finding. Three states are separated that ordinary code mashes together: a genuine zero is a measurement, a missing value means nobody measured, and a value under another key means it was measured and filed elsewhere, which is the case here. Rule: never let a lookup failure become a value; keep missing as missing, print the missing count beside every summary, and find out why before filling anything in. Distinct from Liang, which is about a join that matches too much or too little between records that BOTH EXIST; this one is about nothing coming back at all.
requiredMentions: An absent record is not a zero
