Jerudong International School. It is real and well known, but the source consulted for this page does not cover it, so no claim about it, its curriculum or its outcomes appears anywhere on the page.
Any figure for visitors to Jerudong Park, before or after the change from free admission. None was found and none is estimated.
Any 2021 figure for Kampong Jerudong. The settlement figure available is 2016 and the page labels it as such, while the mukim figure quoted alongside it is 2021.

Any claim that Jerudong is missing from official records. It is fully recorded, under Mukim Sengkurong, and the page says so; the project is about what code does with a failed lookup, not about a gap in the data.

coding-classes-in-as-suwaiq.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma, alongside Cambridge International within the wilayat at Disley Private School and a separate Pakistani curriculum stream at Pakistan School Suwaiq. The page argues that three curricula inside one wilayat is itself the reason a learner record needs an explicit curriculum field rather than an assumption drawn from the place name.
coding-classes-in-as-suwaiq.localProject: Identifiers that lose their leading zero. A 32-village register coded 01 to 32, joined against a survey column that one spreadsheet read as numeric, dropping exactly the nine keys 01 to 09. Assigned to this page and no other: checked against the stable-identifier trap on Ash Sharqiyah North, the visits-against-visitors trap on Al Khuwair and the missing-as-zero trap on Ibra before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Al Suwaiq Industrial City total area of 10 million square metres, inaugurated 2024, targeting food and beverage, pharmaceutical and logistics sectors.

Disley Private School describes itself as the only Cambridge accredited bilingual school in Al Suwaiq, working within the Ministry of Education framework combined with the Cambridge International Curriculum.

The wilayat contains 32 villages including Al Nabrah, Al Mabrah, Al Tharmad, Al Hailain, Al Manfash and Bawarh; it measures roughly 48 km by 80 km and is the largest wilayat in Oman; Al Suwaiq Fort is 60 m by 43 m with three circular towers and one square, restored 1992.
Pakistan School Suwaiq has served the Pakistani community and other expatriate families in As Suwaiq since 1994.

rejectedClaims: A headline population for the wilayat. One published table gives about 200,994 at the 2022 census and the wilayat article gives about 140,577 for 2021. The two could not be reconciled at primary source, so no population figure appears on the page and the National Centre for Statistics and Information is named as the authority.

A count of agricultural villages. One secondary source says the wilayat oversees about 46 agricultural villages while the wilayat article counts 32 villages in total. The page uses only the 32 figure and does not repeat the 46.

coding-classes-in-saham.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma, delivered in government schools across the wilayat. The page argues from distance rather than from curriculum: Saham is about 200 kilometres from Muscat, so the weekly cost of a physical class is a day rather than an evening, and that is the honest case for live online delivery.
coding-classes-in-saham.localProject: A number living inside a text label. Numbered outlet labels across two of Saham's named aflaj, sorted plainly, putting 10 before 2 and moving five of six positions. Assigned to this page and no other: natural sort was checked free against every page in the cluster before it was chosen, unlike the identifier and count-distinct traps which are already taken.

sources.claim: Saham is a coastal town in Al Batinah North between Al Khaburah and Sohar, about 200 km from Muscat; main industries are fishing and farming; the souq was renovated to modern standards in 2018 and holds a livestock market on the seventh day of Dhu al-Hijja; named regions include Majaz, Al-Huwail, Al-Marfa, Al-Hadeeb, Al-Gowaisa, Al-Deel and Hafeet, and the khors Khor Al Milh, Khor AlHimam and Khor AlShiyadi.

Saham souq covers 130,000 square metres; the slaughterhouse opened in 2015; the aflaj Bani Ameer, Al Roodha, Al Mahab and Sheidah and the wadis Aheen, Khour Al Malh and Al Sakahn are named; Al Souq Fort was once the residence of the governor; villages include Sur Al Shiyadi, Sur Al Buloosh, Mukhaileef, Khour Al Hamam and Al Manqel.
Saham is recorded as one of the larger wilayats of Al Batinah North and sits between Al Khaboura and Sohar on the Sea of Oman coast, with lemon production historically exported in quantity.

rejectedClaims: A headline population. Three published figures exist on three different bases: 147,775 for 2017, 165,546 at the 2022 census, and about 122,493 for 2023 on an Omani-citizens-only series. Mixing bases would be worse than omitting the number, so no population appears on the page.

Any statement about the real rotation order of a named falaj. The four falaj names are published; their water shares are not ours to publish, and the outlet numbers in the project are labelled as teaching values.

coding-classes-in-al-amarat.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma, delivered through the 30 schools the wilayat records for more than 25,000 students. The page argues from access rather than curriculum: Al Amarat sits behind a mountain range from Bausher on a road its own residents have campaigned to replace, so a weekly class that depends on that corridor is a weekly risk.
coding-classes-in-al-amarat.localProject: Percentages that are each rounded correctly and do not total 100. Twenty shares across the wilayat's 20 published administrative areas total 100.2 under independent rounding, and largest-remainder apportionment returns them to 100.0 by moving two figures. Assigned to this page and no other: checked against the weighted-average trap on Al Batinah North and Mawaleh, the percentage-wording trap on Al Ghubrah and the base-rate trap on Duqm before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Al Amarat comprises 20 administrative areas, contains 57 valleys and 61 aflaj, produces dates, mangoes and sidr, operates seven factories for plaster and brick, and contains Beit Al Maqam Fort.
30 schools provide educational services to more than 25 thousand students.
Residents have called for a permanent solution to the Amerat-Bausher mountain road, with many arguing that an alternative route, especially a tunnel, is required to connect the two wilayats.
Muscat Governorate consists of six wilayats: Muscat, Muttrah, Al Seeb, Qurayat, Bausher and Al Amerat.

rejectedClaims: The wilayat area. One source gives 925 square kilometres for Al Amarat and another gives the same 925 for Liwa in Al Batinah North. Those cannot both be right as stated, so neither page carries an area and both name the National Centre for Statistics and Information as the authority.

A single headline population. Published figures range from about 69,132 in a 2016 breakdown to roughly 139,755 at the 2022 census, and one secondary source prints "121,103 thousand people", which cannot be right on any reading. The page states the range with both years attached rather than picking one figure.

That the Wadi Adai to Al Amerat link is a tunnel. It is a mountain road corridor. Residents have argued a tunnel is what is needed, which is a call rather than a built fact, and the page words it that way.

coding-classes-in-rustaq.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page does not argue from curriculum at all. It argues that Rustaq already runs a scheduling system older than the word, with fixed slots, a repeating cycle, an elected administrator and an audit role, so a learner here does not need the concept explained, only the notation.
coding-classes-in-rustaq.localProject: Modular arithmetic on a repeating cycle. A 48-athar day inside an eight day dawaran is 384 turns; naive division places 8 of them on the wrong day and its worst answer is day 9 of an eight day cycle. Assigned to this page and no other: modulo and cyclic scheduling were checked free across every page in the cluster, and the elapsed-time trap already used by Ibri and Nizwa was avoided deliberately.

sources.claim: Falaj Al-Muyassar is one of the five aflaj UNESCO inscribed in 2006, is a Dawoodi falaj reaching 50 metres depth with a flow of 210 litres per second, and is among the most significant aflaj in Wilayat Al Rustaq.

Falaj water is shared by athar of 30 minutes on a rotation, the dawaran, typically of 7 to 14 days; a baddah is 12 hours or 24 athar; the falaj is run by an elected wakil with arifs regulating timing and a qabidh keeping financial records, and night timing is read from known stars.

Al Rustaq Fort dates to the 13th century and was expanded by the Ya'aruba dynasty between 1624 and 1649, with four towers the tallest over 18 metres; Al Hazm Castle was built by Imam Sultan bin Saif al Yarubi in the early 18th century; Wadi Al Hoqain lies 45 km from the centre with year-round streams and Niyabat Al Hoqain about 150 km from Muscat.

Ain Al Kasfa lies about 1,500 metres west of Rustaq Castle, irrigates the surrounding palm farms, and carries the largest water volume of any spring in northern Oman; an Abbasid governor tried to bury it and the water reappeared about ten metres from the original source.

rejectedClaims: The actual rotation order or share allocation of Falaj Al-Muyassar or any other named falaj. Shares belong to the shareholders and are not published; the eight day cycle in the project is chosen from inside the documented seven to fourteen day range and is labelled as such on the page.
A population figure for the wilayat. The 2022 census gives about 129,050, but this page makes no argument that depends on it, so it is not stated rather than stated decoratively.

coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-ali.market: Jalan Bani Bu Ali, Ash Sharqiyah South
coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-ali.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from currency rather than curriculum: the Omani rial divides into 1000 baisa, so every price in this trading town carries three decimal places, and the two-decimal money advice that dominates programming writing is a digit short before it starts.
coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-ali.localProject: Money in binary floating point, in a three decimal currency. A six line Friday souq basket totals 11.325000000000001 as a float against 11.325 exactly, prints as 11.325 either way, and fails the equality check a till runs at closing. Counting the same money in whole baisa passes. Assigned to this page and no other: floating point money was checked free across every page in the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Jami Al-Hamoda in Jalan Bani Bu Ali has 52 separate mud-brick domes of equal size with a falaj running beneath it, openings called mabariq, 24 cylinders, five corridors, capacity for more than 700 worshippers, was built almost 500 years ago, and is locally called Al Qibab or the Mosque of Domes.

Jalan Bani Bu Ali is a commercial town and tourist destination in Ash Sharqiyah South with many shops and supermarkets, a traditional souq about 1 km south of the centre trading on Friday mornings, sand dunes with standing water pools, a distinct summer rainy season unusual for Oman, and was the site of an 1821 British East India Company expedition.
The mosque is located in the Wilayat of Jalan Bani Bu Ali in Ash Sharqiyah South Governorate and serves as a centre for study and preservation of the Holy Qur'an.

rejectedClaims: An exact founding date for Jami Al-Hamoda. Sources say it was built almost 500 years ago, which is an approximation, and the page repeats it as an approximation rather than converting it into a year.
A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 117,730 for the wilayat, but no argument on this page depends on it, so it is omitted rather than used as decoration.

coding-classes-in-al-musanaah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the wilayat's sporting infrastructure rather than its schools: Al Musanaah hosts international championship sailing, so results here are recorded under published rules that anybody can check, which is what lets the project show a right answer beside a wrong one instead of asserting which is which.
coding-classes-in-al-musanaah.localProject: A missing value inside an aggregate, in a sport that already ruled on it. A six race series where a boat sailing four races comes first on an average that skips the blanks and last under World Sailing's low point rule of entries plus one. Assigned to this page and no other: deliberately distinct from Ibra's missing-as-zero trap, because skipping is the more dangerous failure and produces a plausible answer where zeroing produces an obviously silly one.

sources.claim: Al-Musannah Sports City covers 1,000,000 square metres with capacity for 5,000 athletes, was built between 2008 and 2010 and opened on 8 December 2010, hosting the opening ceremony of the second Asian Beach Games held from 8 to 16 December 2010.

The inaugural World Sailing Inclusion Championships were held at Mussanah from 30 November to 8 December 2025 with 154 athletes entered, across four classes: Hansa 303, RS Venture Connect, ILCA 6 and FarEast 28R.

The Asian Sailing Federation selected Oman Sail's Mussanah Sailing School as a High Performance Centre; the school sits at the marina and water sports centre at the Barcelo Mussanah Resort about 85 km north of Muscat, with a 20 metre wide slipway, a boatyard and docking for around 400 boats.

Al-Musannah is a coastal town in Al Batinah South Governorate with a 2020 census population of 99,204, one of six wilayats in the governorate alongside Rustaq, Al Awabi, Nakhal, Wadi Al Maawil and Barka.

rejectedClaims: Any claim that the race series in the project is a real regatta result. It is a teaching example and the page labels it as one. Only the scoring rule is real.

Attendance or entry figures for events at the venue beyond the 154 athletes reported for the 2025 championships. Other event totals could not be confirmed at first-party source and are therefore not stated.

coding-classes-in-bahla.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from distance and from subject rather than from curriculum: Bahla is about 200 kilometres from Muscat and 40 from Nizwa, and its published record is unusually full of measurements of awkwardly shaped things, which is the case data work handles worst.
coding-classes-in-bahla.localProject: Perimeter against area, and its software cousin the bounding box. Twelve kilometres of oasis wall enclosing anywhere from 11.46 to 0.30 square kilometres depending on shape, a spread of 39 times, and an eight-vertex plot whose bounding box area is 98.6 per cent too big against the shoelace formula. Assigned to this page and no other. The obvious Bahla hook was the Nabhani dates in AH and AD, which was rejected because Nizwa forty kilometres away already owns calendar conversion.

sources.claim: Bahla Fort was the first site in Oman inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, in 1987; it covers about 9,822 square metres, is irregular in shape, and the oasis walls around it extend for more than 12 kilometres.

Bahla lies about 40 km from Nizwa and 200 km from Muscat at about 550 m elevation; the fort is 13th century with adobe walls and towers on stone foundations inside a 12 km fortified wall; the Nabhani dynasty ruled from the mid 12th to the end of the 15th century with Bahla as second and later main capital; pottery is dated back as early as 2500 BC; Jabrin Castle lies 5 km south west, built under Al Ya'ruba in the mid 17th century; the Friday Mosque carries a sculpted mihrab of roughly the 14th century.
Bahla Fort is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, reference 433.

rejectedClaims: A headline population. One source gives 85,000 and the 2022 census table gives 96,415, and no argument on this page depends on either, so neither is stated.

A precise date for the Friday Mosque mihrab. The record says approximately the 14th century and the page keeps the approximation rather than converting it into a year that would read better and mean less.

coding-classes-in-al-mudhaibi.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from scale rather than curriculum: Al Mudhaibi is the largest wilayat in its governorate at roughly 3,000 square kilometres with two niabas and settlements of wildly unequal size, so no single physical location could serve it and no careless average can describe it.
coding-classes-in-al-mudhaibi.localProject: The average of several rates against the overall rate. Five settlements, four small and one holding 91 per cent of the learners: the mean of the five rates is 77.0 per cent and total passes over total entries is 57.5, a gap of 19.5 percentage points. Assigned to this page and no other: checked free across the cluster, and kept clear of the percentage-wording trap on Al Ghubrah and the share-rounding trap on Al Amarat.

sources.claim: Al Mudhaibi is the largest wilayat in Ash Sharqiyah with an estimated area of about 3,000 square kilometres, holds the two niabas Sinaw and Samad Ash Shan, and its villages include Al Sudairah, Barzman, Al Zahib, Al Alia, Bani Difaa and the Al-Dhaqiq area between Lazq and Al Maysar; agriculture is the first craft, with palm, lemon, alfalfa and vegetables.
Samad al-Shan is noted for ancient Umm al-Nar period sites dated to roughly 2500 to 2000 BCE.
Suq Sinaw is among the most popular souqs in Oman, selling dresses, khanjars and jewellery.

rejectedClaims: A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 92,193 for the wilayat, but the page argues from area and from the inequality between settlements rather than from a total, so a headline population would be decoration.
Any real per-settlement pass rate. No public per-village result file exists, so the counts in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such on the page.

coding-classes-in-al-khaburah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from dispersion rather than curriculum: 198 villages spread from the coast to Adh Dhahirah and about 176 kilometres from Muscat means no physical centre could be convenient for more than a handful of them.
coding-classes-in-al-khaburah.localProject: The sum of the peaks against the peak of the sums. A modelled year across the wilayat's 198 villages, each with its own busy season: summing the individual peaks overstates the real system maximum by about 100 per cent, and zero of the 198 villages peaked on the day the whole wilayat did. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Al Khaburah has 198 villages including Al Sihra, Al Qala, Khadra Al Makatim, Sanaa Bani Ghafir and Miha Bani Kayoum; it lies about 176 km from Muscat and stretches from Saham in the north to As Suwaiq in the south and Adh Dhahirah in the west; residents work in agriculture, sheep herding, fishing, khanjar making, weaving, pottery, copper and leather.
Al Khabourah Castle is the most famous of the wilayat's forts and castles and dates to the 19th century AD.
Al Khaburah is a wilayat of Al Batinah North Governorate in Oman.

rejectedClaims: A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 89,971, but the page argues from the village count and their independence rather than from a total, so a headline population would be decoration.
Any real per-village demand or consumption figure. No public daily record exists, so the series in the project are modelled and are labelled as modelled on the page.

coding-classes-in-shinas.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the border rather than the curriculum: Shinas overlooks some of the Sultanate's most important land crossings and runs a port trading with Iran, so its records are bilingual by necessity and its software has to hold two scripts rather than one.
coding-classes-in-shinas.localProject: A field measured in characters against a field measured in bytes. Place names from the wilayat in Latin and Arabic through a twenty byte limit: every Latin name survives, a fourteen character Arabic name loses three letters, and a twenty character Arabic name loses half. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Shinas is one of the six coastal wilayats of Al Batinah North, bordered to the north by the United Arab Emirates and overlooking some of the Sultanate's most important land crossings, with fertile agricultural plains using aflaj irrigation.
Shinas Port handled 88,000 tonnes over a twelve month period, mainly building materials, food, live animals and chemical and pharmaceutical products traded between Oman and Iran.
Traditional dhows still sail from Shinas and fresh fish is caught for supply to local markets.

rejectedClaims: A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 88,317, but the page argues from the border position and the bilingual record rather than from a total.
Any claim about the port's capacity or its peak throughput. The 88,000 tonne figure is a twelve month throughput, and the page says so rather than letting it be read as a capacity.

coding-classes-in-samail.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the shape of the wilayat rather than from curriculum: 55 settlements strung along a wadi that divides the Hajar into two ranges means no single meeting point is convenient for most of them.
coding-classes-in-samail.localProject: The header row counted as data. A list of the wilayat's 55 villages read without skipping the first line yields 56, one of them named village; the mosque total stays correct at 388 either way and the average per village moves from 7.05 to 6.93. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Samail lies in Ad Dakhiliyah beside the Hajar Mountains; Wadi Samail is one of the largest wadis and the Samail Gap divides the Hajar into eastern and western subranges; the wilayat holds 55 villages and towns and more than 300 mosques.
The Mazin bin Ghadouba Mosque in Samail is considered the oldest mosque in Oman and was built by Mazin bin Ghadouba in 627 AD.
Mazin bin Ghadouba is recorded as the first Muslim in Oman and the mosque is described as the first mosque of Oman.

rejectedClaims: A headline population. One source gives about 40,000 for the wilayat and the 2022 census table gives about 87,997. The two could not be reconciled, so no population appears and the page argues from the settlement count instead.
Any per-village mosque figure. Only the wilayat totals are published, so the per-village numbers in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such.

coding-classes-in-izki.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the length of the record rather than from curriculum: a falaj with more than two millennia behind it is the clearest case anywhere of observations that were never evenly sampled.
coding-classes-in-izki.localProject: Readings taken at irregular intervals, averaged as though evenly spaced. Six falaj readings across fifty four years, five of them in the first five: the plain mean is 87.7 and the time weighted mean is 95.2 on the same six numbers. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster, and kept clear of the elapsed-time work on Ibri and the seasonality work on Salalah.

sources.claim: Izki is popularly claimed to be the oldest town in Oman and was notorious for intrigues between the Yamani and the Nizari; the Yamani are southern Arabs claiming origins in Yemen who migrated to Oman between the 2nd century BC and the 2nd century AD, and the Nizari are northern Arabs who migrated from what is now the Nejd.

Izki is celebrated as Oman's oldest city on the evidence of its ancient aflaj and the twin walled towns of Izki or al-Yemen and al-Nizar; Falaj al Malaki is one of the five largest aflaj in Oman with a history spanning over two millennia.
Al Malki Falaj is shared by Nazar village and is one of the important water sources in the area; Harat Al Yemen is the old quarter walked by visitors.

rejectedClaims: That Izki IS the oldest town in Oman. The sources say popularly claimed and celebrated as, which is a claim about a reputation rather than a settled dating, and the page repeats it in those terms.

A population figure and any real flow series for the falaj. The 2022 census gives about 66,034 for the wilayat, which nothing here argues from, and no public flow record exists, so the project readings are labelled as teaching values.

coding-classes-in-liwa.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from a documented naming discrepancy rather than from curriculum: the largest facility in the wilayat carries the neighbouring wilayat's name in its own published description, which makes it the clearest available case of a location that cannot be inferred from a label.
coding-classes-in-liwa.localProject: Deriving a location from a name. Five records through a name-based wilayat guess: two are misfiled, and because the port is the only row carrying weight, a million tonnes a week moves from Liwa to Sohar with nothing raised. Assigned to this page and no other; distinct from the stable-identifier work on Ash Sharqiyah North because this is about inferring an ATTRIBUTE from a name rather than about the identity of the key itself.
requiredMentions: National Centre for Statistics and Information

sources.claim: SOHAR Port and Freezone is a deep sea port and adjacent free zone located in Liwa, Al Batinah North, despite the name suggesting otherwise, and the port handles over one million tonnes of sea cargo each week and around 3,500 ships a year.
Liwa is a wilayat of Al Batinah North lying north of Sohar and overlooking the Gulf of Oman to its east, distributed over 51 villages.
From the towers of Liwa Fort a visitor can see many of the wilayat's villages, including the coastal village of Harmul and its mangrove trees.

rejectedClaims: The wilayat area. Two published sources give 925 square kilometres for Liwa and the same 925 for Al Amarat in Muscat Governorate, which cannot both be right as stated. Neither page states an area, and both name the National Centre for Statistics and Information as the authority.
A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 63,292, but the page argues from the naming discrepancy rather than from a total.

coding-classes-in-qurayyat.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from inequality of scale rather than curriculum: a fishing coast running from a town fleet down to three boat landings is the clearest available case of why a percentage ranking rewards being small rather than being busy.
coding-classes-in-qurayyat.localProject: A rate computed on a tiny denominator. Four landing points given one extra boat each: the three boat harbour posts 33.3 per cent, the town posts 0.6, and the town would need about sixty more boats to match the headline. Assigned to this page and no other; distinct from the share-rounding trap on Al Amarat and the average-of-rates trap on Al Mudhaibi because this is about the size of the base rather than the method of aggregation.

sources.claim: The Bimmah Sinkhole is in the Dabab area of Wilayat Qurayyat on the northeast coast of Muscat Governorate, about 600 metres inland, is a pool about 65 feet deep confirmed by geologists as a sinkhole though local legend holds a meteorite made it, and holds fresh and salt water in roughly equal proportions giving it a turquoise hue.
Quriyat is known for its traditional fishing boats and views over the sea, and its past was marked by fierce resistance to Portuguese invasion; it is today described as a quiet fishing village.
Muscat Governorate consists of six wilayats: Muscat, Muttrah, Al Seeb, Qurayat, Bausher and Al Amerat.

rejectedClaims: That a meteorite formed the Bimmah Sinkhole. Geologists have confirmed it is a sinkhole; the meteorite account is a local legend and the page presents it as one rather than choosing between them silently.

A population figure and any real per-landing-point boat count. The 2022 census gives about 63,006 for the wilayat, which nothing here argues from, and no public boat record exists, so the project counts are labelled as teaching values.

coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-hassan.market: Jalan Bani Bu Hassan, Ash Sharqiyah South
coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-hassan.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the wilayat's own name rather than from curriculum: it and its neighbour differ only in the final word, and its fort answers to two names, so it carries both halves of the key problem at once in a way no invented example could.
coding-classes-in-jalan-bani-bu-hassan.localProject: A key built by squashing and truncating a name. Sweeping the width from eight to fourteen characters across Jalan Bani Bu Hassan and Jalan Bani Bu Ali: they collide at every width up to eleven and separate at twelve, so one character is the entire safety margin. Paired with the reverse fault, one fort under two names. Assigned to this page and no other; distinct from the stable-identifier work on Ash Sharqiyah North because this is about the WIDTH of a derived key rather than about choosing one.

sources.claim: Jalan Bani Bu Hassan Fort, sometimes also known as Al Muhaywil Castle, is in Ash Sharqiyah South; it is said to have been founded in the 9th century during the reign of Al-Muhanna bin Jayfar as Imam of Oman, was thoroughly rebuilt during the reign of Thuwaini bin Said, Sultan from 1856 to 1866, and served as the main fortification in the area and the home and office of the local wali.
Jalan Bani Bu Hassan is a wilayat of Ash Sharqiyah South Governorate in Oman.
Ash Sharqiyah South contains the wilayats Sur, Jalan Bani Bu Ali, Jalan Bani Bu Hassan, Al Kamil Wal Wafi and Masirah.

rejectedClaims: A firm 9th century founding date for the fort. The sources say it is said to have been founded then, which is a tradition rather than a dated record, and the page keeps that wording. The 1856 to 1866 reign under which it was rebuilt is the firmer date and the page leans on that one.
A population figure. The 2022 census gives about 50,755 for the wilayat, but the page argues entirely from the names rather than from any total.

coding-classes-in-bidiyah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the shape of the wilayat rather than from curriculum: a settlement that works as the entrance to a sand sea is a route rather than a centre, and teaching that travels to the learner is the only arrangement that treats the whole route alike.
coding-classes-in-bidiyah.localProject: A threshold stored as a value. Twelve dune heights capped at 100 because the source said over 100 metres: the mean falls from 97.8 to 84.7, the maximum from 156 to 100, the standard deviation from 33.6 to 19.9, and the count of dunes above 100 metres falls from six to zero. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Bidiya is a wilayat of North Al Sharqiyah about 230 kilometres southeast of Muscat, holding plains, mountains, dunes, oases, aflaj and natural springs, and sitting on the edge of the Wahiba Sands.
Dunes in the Wahiba Sands rise over 100 metres high, and the sand sea covers roughly 1,500 square kilometres.
Bidiya Sands is also known as Wahiba Sands, and the easiest entrances are at Bidiyah Castle, reached by gravel road before the sand tracks, and at Al Wasil.

rejectedClaims: A headline population for the wilayat. Figures circulating for Bidiya could not be traced to a census table, so none appears and the page argues from terrain instead.

Any individual dune height. Only the over 100 metres description is published, so the twelve heights inside the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A road distance to anywhere other than Muscat. The 230 kilometre figure is the only one traced to a source, and it is itself rounded.

coding-classes-in-al-kamil-wal-wafi.market: Al Kamil Wal Wafi, Ash Sharqiyah South
coding-classes-in-al-kamil-wal-wafi.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from settlement structure rather than curriculum: a population divided across about 40 clusters has no centre that is fair to all of them, so teaching that arrives over a connection is the only arrangement that reaches every cluster on equal terms.
coding-classes-in-al-kamil-wal-wafi.localProject: A substring match standing in for an exact one. The wilayat's clusters include both Tawi and Tawi Hatim; querying Tawi with contains returns two rows and 2,630 against a correct one row and 780, which is 3.37 times too high, while querying the longer name is always correct. Assigned to this page and no other; checked free across the cluster before it was chosen.

sources.claim: Al Kamil Wal Wafi is a wilayat of the South Al Sharqiyah governorate at about 22 degrees 13 minutes north and 59 degrees 12 minutes east, bordered by Wadi Bani Khalid, Sur and a neighbouring wilayat, with about 40 clusters as its population centres including Al-Kamil, Al-Wafi, Tawi Hatim, Tahwa and Tawi.

Al-Kamil wa al-Wafi is filed under Ash Sharqiyah South Governorate in a population statistics database independent of the encyclopedia entry, which is the second reference used to settle the governorate question.
Al Kamil Wal Wafi is recorded as a named place feature in Oman with its own location record.

rejectedClaims: A population for the wilayat or for any of its clusters. No census table could be traced in this session, so no population appears on the page and the five figures inside the project are labelled teaching values in three separate places.

The governorate given by a third source. One reference placed this wilayat in Ash Sharqiyah North. Two others place it in the South and those two are followed, with the disagreement stated on the page rather than concealed.
A count of the wilayat's settlements stated as exact. The published figure is about 40 clusters and the word about is kept everywhere it appears.

coding-classes-in-bidbid.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the wilayat's settlement pattern rather than from curriculum: towers scattered across villages nobody has finished counting means learners scattered the same way, and a lesson delivered over a connection is what reaches all of them equally.
coding-classes-in-bidbid.localProject: A rate built on a denominator nobody published. Bidbid's 40 towers are recorded; the number of villages is not. Across plausible village counts from 8 to 35 the towers-per-village rate runs from 5.00 to 1.14, a 4.4-fold spread in which every value is arithmetically correct. Assigned to this page and no other; deliberately not a text-matching fault, to keep it clear of the substring and spelling-variant projects on neighbouring pages.

sources.claim: Bidbid Fort was among the first restored with local construction materials including palm tree trunks supporting parts of the roof; the wilayat includes 40 towers scattered in different villages, a wadi dividing its banks into two parts, and aflaj including the Eastern Hammam Falaj, a western hot falaj from the mountain heights, Falaj Al Rahah and Falaj Al Hakka.
People come to Fanja's souq from neighbouring villages as buyers and sellers of locally made handicrafts.
Bidbid is a wilayat of the Ad Dakhiliyah governorate of Oman.

rejectedClaims: A village count for Bidbid, which is the whole point of the page. No source consulted gives one, so no towers-per-village rate is stated as fact anywhere and the six values in the project table are labelled assumptions in the table itself.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears.

Fanja's governorate as given by one population database, whose own pages place Fanja under Bidbid in more than one governorate. Bidbid is a wilayat of Ad Dakhiliyah; the disagreement is described on the page as evidence rather than repeated as fact.

coding-classes-in-adam.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the size of the town rather than from curriculum: a place this small cannot host a specialist teacher for every subject a learner might want, and delivering the lesson over a connection is what removes that ceiling.
coding-classes-in-adam.localProject: The word about does not survive arithmetic. Ahmad bin Said was born in Adam in 1694 and the dynasty has ruled since about 1749; subtracting gives 55, printed with no hedge. Under readings of about at plus or minus 2, 5 and 10 years the honest answer is a window 4, 10 or 20 years wide. Separately, around 120 houses plus 6 exact towers is uncertain by exactly what around was already worth, so the exact figure adds no precision. Assigned to this page and no other. Distinct from the Bidiyah project, which censors a value at a threshold rather than losing precision in an operation.

sources.claim: Ahmad bin Said, founder of the Al Busaidi dynasty, was born in the city of Adam, Oman, in 1694.
The Al Bu Said dynasty has ruled Oman since about 1749, when Ahmad ibn Said, governor of Suhar, displaced the Yarubids and became imam of Oman, with authority extending to Zanzibar, Pemba and Kilwa.
Harat al Busaid is ranked one of the oldest lanes in Adam, is where Ahmed bin Said was born, and has around 120 old houses protected by 6 defensive towers.

rejectedClaims: A width for the word about. No source states whether about 1749 means within two years or within ten, so the three readings in the project table are labelled illustrative in the table, in the pitfalls note and in the FAQ.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears and the page argues from the size of the historic quarter instead.
A death date for Ahmad bin Said. Figures circulate but none was verified at a primary source in this session, so the page uses only the birth year and the dynasty date.

coding-classes-in-nakhal.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the wilayat's hydrology rather than from curriculum: settlement here follows the irrigation channels, so the shape of the place has no natural centre and teaching delivered over a connection does not need one.
coding-classes-in-nakhal.localProject: A total that includes its own source. The Al Thowarah springs run about 300 metres from Silud Mountain before branching into Falaj Kabbah and Falaj As Sarooj. With a spring of 60 l/s, 3 lost on the way and branches of 33 and 24, the three-row sum is 117 against a true 60, which is 95% too high and, because of the loss, not exactly double, so the one sanity check a reviewer would run comes back clean. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: The Al Thowarah hot springs gush all year round from Silud Mountain and flow from the valley for a distance of 300 metres before branching into two tributaries, Falaj Kabbah and Falaj As Sarooj, on which Wilayat Nakhal depends to irrigate its cultivated lands.
Nakhal Fort is surrounded by a date palm oasis set against mountainous terrain.
Al Thowarah is a hot spring located near Nakhal Fort in Oman.

rejectedClaims: Any flow rate for the spring or either tributary. No public gauging figures were found, so the litres per second in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears and the page argues from the shape of the irrigation instead.
A temperature for the springs. Figures circulate but none was verified at a primary source in this session, so the page says only that the water is warm year round.

coding-classes-in-al-hamra.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from terrain rather than curriculum: villages terraced up a mountainside are separated by gradient rather than by map distance, and a lesson delivered over a connection is the only one indifferent to how steep the road is.
coding-classes-in-al-hamra.localProject: Inclusive and exclusive band edges, with a real value sitting on one. Misfat Al Abriyeen is published at exactly 900 metres, a band edge. Ten elevations across four bands under three defensible rules give totals of 14, 9 and 10 out of 10 villages: both ends closed overcounts by 40 per cent, half open upward silently drops the highest village, and only one rule reconciles. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Misfat al Abriyeen is a village in the wilayah of Al Hamra, located in an oasis at 900 metres, or 3,000 feet, above sea level in the western Hajar mountains, with an extensive falaj water canalization system dating back more than 2,000 years; the village gives its name to the Al Abri tribe.
Misfat Al Abriyeen is widely described as a mud village in Oman and remains inhabited and farmed.
Al Hamra and Misfat Al Abriyin have been the subject of documentation, heritage management and tourism development planning work.

rejectedClaims: Elevations for any village other than Misfat Al Abriyeen. No per-village elevation table for the wilayat was found, so the other nine figures in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears and the page argues from terrain instead.
A precise age for the falaj. The published claim is more than 2,000 years, which is a lower bound, and the page keeps it as one rather than converting it to a date.

coding-classes-in-dima-wa-attayeen.market: Dima Wa Attayeen, Ash Sharqiyah North
coding-classes-in-dima-wa-attayeen.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from settlement pattern rather than curriculum: a population spread along wadis in dozens of small villages has no convenient common meeting point, so teaching that travels to the learner is what reaches the whole wilayat.
coding-classes-in-dima-wa-attayeen.localProject: An empty cell is not a zero. Across the wilayat's some 51 villages, 40 report water sources totalling 140, 6 are surveyed and genuinely dry, and 5 are never reached. The mean per village is 2.75, 3.04 or 3.50 depending on the denominator, a 27 per cent swing; the count of villages with no active source is 6 or 11 depending purely on whether blanks are read as zeros. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Wilayat Dima W'attayeen is a wilayat of the North Sharqiyah Governorate, per the governorate's own official site.

Dima W'attayeen borders Qurayat to the north, Ibra to the south, Al Qabil and Bidiya to the east and Al Mudhaibi and Bidbid to the west; it is mountainous and abundantly blessed with water, and the large majority of its residents live in some 51 villages which mainly dot the fringes of the wilayat's major wadis.
Arabian Tahr have been sighted in the Wilayat of Dima W'attayeen.

rejectedClaims: Per-village water source counts. No published survey exists, so every figure in the project is a teaching value and is labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
The village count stated without its hedge. The source says some 51 villages and the word some is kept on every appearance.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears and the page argues from the settlement pattern instead.
Two of the three sources here come from the same publisher. That is stated rather than presented as three independent confirmations; the governorate site is the independent one.

coding-classes-in-yanqul.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from what is coming to the wilayat rather than from curriculum: a copper project due to open in early 2027 will need people who can already handle data, and teaching delivered over a connection does not wait for a training centre to be built first.
coding-classes-in-yanqul.localProject: Truncation is one-sided and rounding is not. Twelve monthly tonnages with one decimal each total 246.4; rounding gives 246.0 and truncating gives 240.0, so the truncation error is sixteen times worse from identical inputs. None of the twelve truncation errors is positive, mean minus 0.53 a row, so it drifts by roughly half a unit per row indefinitely, while rounding error changes sign and cancels at minus 0.03. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: The Mazoon Copper Project is the largest integrated copper concentrate production project in Oman, covering 20 square kilometres, consisting of five open-pit mines with an estimated 22.9 million tons of copper ore reserves, and is anticipated to commence operations in early 2027.
Yanqul is a wilayat of Ad Dhahirah Governorate in the northwest of Oman, near the border with the United Arab Emirates.
A gold mine location is recorded at Yanqul in Ad Dhahirah Governorate.

rejectedClaims: Any monthly or annual production tonnage. The mine has not started, so all twelve monthly figures in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A copper metal figure derived from the ore reserve. 22.9 million tons is ore, not metal, and no grade was traced in this session, so no metal tonnage is stated anywhere on the page.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears.
A precise start date. The published wording is early 2027 and that hedge is kept.

coding-classes-in-manah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the wilayat's form rather than from curriculum: Manah is old quarters, villages and farmland rather than a single centre, so there is no address convenient to everyone and a lesson delivered over a connection does not need one.
coding-classes-in-manah.localProject: A fast search that silently requires an order nobody supplied. Harat Al Bilad holds 376 houses; binary search over the ordered list finds 376 of 376, and over the same records as recorded it finds 8, reporting 368 present houses as absent, a 97.9 per cent failure rate. It answers in about nine steps either way and raises no error or warning at all. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Harat Al Bilad in the Wilayat of Manah is one of Oman's largest ancient archaeological neighbourhoods, containing 376 houses and nearly 250 wells dating back nine centuries, and was the seat of an active scientific movement where many books and Fiqh encyclopedias were reproduced.
Fiqain Castle, in Al Fiqain village, was built some 400 years ago and its position affords views of the old residential quarters, palm groves and farms of the village.
Manah is a wilayat of the Ad Dakhiliyah governorate of Oman.

rejectedClaims: A register of individual house identifiers. None is published, so the identifiers used in the exercise are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
An exact well count. The published figure is nearly 250 and the hedge is kept everywhere it appears.
An exact age for Fiqain Castle. The published wording is some 400 years ago, kept as written rather than converted into a construction date.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears.

coding-classes-in-al-qabil.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the wilayat's geography rather than from curriculum: a population of just under 25,000 split between desert edge and mountain has no convenient common meeting point, and a lesson delivered over a connection is the same length from either side.
coding-classes-in-al-qabil.localProject: Free-text spellings, and the limits of cleaning them. The oasis here is published as Shenah or Shanah. Across 400 hand-typed visit records under six strings, a naive GROUP BY returns six rows with a largest of 168, understating by 58 per cent; trimming and case folding collapses six rows to three and leaves the best row at 198 of 400, still 50 per cent short, because e against a is a genuine spelling difference. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Al-Qabil is a province in the governorate of Ash-Sharqiyah North in Oman with a population of 24,824 recorded in the 2020 Omani census, located at the northwest corner of the sand desert in eastern Oman; the oasis of Shenah or Shanah, 13 kilometres northeast of Battin and 30 kilometres northeast of Ibra in the eastern Hajar Mountains, has the largest concentration of beehive tombs in Oman, dating to the third millennium BCE.
Al Qabil is presented as a desert destination in Ash Sharqiyah North that is being opened up to visitors.
Ash Sharqiyah North is presented as a destination region of Oman on the national tourism site.

rejectedClaims: The area of the wilayat. The available figure is given as 1,632 kilometres with 1,014 miles in brackets, and neither is a unit of area. Converting it to square kilometres would mean publishing a number no source stated, so no area appears on the page and the FAQ explains the omission.
Visitor numbers for the oasis. None were found, so the 400 records in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A single correct spelling of the oasis name. Both Shenah and Shanah are in circulation and the page treats neither as the error.

coding-classes-in-taqah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from position rather than curriculum: Taqah is close enough to a city to be overlooked and far enough from it to be underserved, and teaching delivered over a connection takes the commute out of the decision.
coding-classes-in-taqah.localProject: One trend line fitted straight across a break in the subject itself. Khor Rori was an open estuary and a working frankincense harbour and is now barred. Across nine century buckets a single least-squares line gives minus 2.08 per century, while the first four centuries rise at plus 8.70 and the last five fall at minus 8.50: the single summary has the sign backwards for nearly half the period and understates the collapse fourfold. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Khor Rori is a bar-built estuary at the mouth of Wadi Darbat in Dhofar, a major breeding ground for birds, which acted as an important harbour for the frankincense trade when it was an open estuary, and is best known for the ruins of the ancient fortified port city of Sumhuram on the eastern bank, with activity recorded from the fourth century BC to the fifth century AD.
Khor Rori is described as an important heritage reserve in Dhofar.
Taqah is an ancient fishing village with a castle, Taqah Castle.

rejectedClaims: Any per-century measure of activity at Khor Rori. No such series is published, so the nine figures in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.

A date for the closing of the estuary mouth. The sources describe the site as a bar-built estuary and put its harbour role in the past tense, but no year was traced, so the page places the turning point inside the invented series only.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears.

coding-classes-in-dhank.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from terrain rather than curriculum: a wilayat ringed by mountains is one where travelling to a lesson costs more than the lesson, and a connection removes that cost from the decision.
coding-classes-in-dhank.localProject: A many-to-many relationship squeezed into one column. Dhank is known for three crafts and households practise more than one. Across 60 households, 26 of them multi-craft, exact matching on a comma-joined column reports leather at 14 against a true 34, understating by 59 per cent, with rose water 63 per cent low and honey 67 per cent low; meanwhile the three true counts sum to 91 against 60 households, overstating by 52 per cent. The same file is badly low one way and badly high the other. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: The Wilayat of Dhank is located in the centre of Al Dhahirah Governorate, takes its name from its odd topographic features with mountains surrounding all sides, borders Al Buraimi on the northwest, Ibri on the southwest and Yanqul on the east, has many valleys such as Wadi Al Fateh and Wadi Qumeirah, and is known for traditional crafts such as tanning leather, extracting rose water and breeding honey bees.
The falaj of Dhank is a noted feature of the wilayat.
Dhank is a wilayat of the Ad Dhahirah Governorate of Oman.

rejectedClaims: Any craft survey figures. None is published, so the 60 households and their combinations are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A complete list of the wilayat's valleys. The sources name Wadi Al Fateh and Wadi Qumeirah as examples among many, and the page treats them as a sample rather than a list.
A population for the wilayat. No census table could be traced in this session, so none appears and the page argues from terrain and craft instead.

coding-classes-in-wadi-al-maawil.market: Wadi Al Maawil, Al Batinah South
coding-classes-in-wadi-al-maawil.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the shape of the wilayat rather than from curriculum: more than fifteen fortified sites means settlements spread through the wadis, so no single meeting point suits most of them and a lesson that travels is what reaches all of them alike.
coding-classes-in-wadi-al-maawil.localProject: The famous example mistaken for the typical one. Over 15 castles stand in the wilayat and Al Safala Castle carries its emblem; scaling that one across fifteen gives 27,000 square metres against a true 5,740, which is 370 per cent too high, while scaling the median gives 3,900, 32 per cent too low. Al Safala alone is 31 per cent of the total and only 4 of 15 sites exceed the mean, with mean 383 against median 260. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Within the boundary of Wadi al Maawil stand over 15 castles, among them Al Safala Castle which takes centre stage and dons the emblem of this ancient wilayat; skilled craftsmen there continue to craft daggers, jewellery, pottery and palm fronds.
Wadi Al Maawil has opened a heritage walkway.
Wadi Al Maawil is a province of Al Batinah South Governorate with a population of 20,206 recorded in 2020.

rejectedClaims: A single population figure. One reference gives 20,206 for the 2020 census and a population database gives 20,174 for the same census. Both appear on the page and neither is adopted as the figure.
Floor areas for any castle. No survey was found, so all fifteen areas in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
An exact castle count. The published figure is over 15, so fifteen is used as the smallest number consistent with the source rather than as a count.

coding-classes-in-al-awabi.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the shape of the valley rather than from curriculum: a wilayat strung along twenty six kilometres of single wadi has no midpoint that is convenient for both ends, and a lesson delivered over a connection costs the same at either.
coding-classes-in-al-awabi.localProject: A straight line between two endpoints that are both correct. Wadi Bani Kharus runs 26 km with limestone from 90 million years old at the entrance to 600 million years in the distant parts; linear interpolation reproduces both endpoints exactly and is worst at 8 km in, saying 247 Ma where the rock is 145 Ma, an error of 102 Ma or 70 per cent of the true age there and a fifth of the whole 510 Ma range. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Wadi Bani Kharus is a valley in Wilayat Al-Awabi, part of the western Al Hajar range, twenty six km long with a southwestern orientation; the limestone formations range from 90 million years old at the entrance of the wadi to 600 million years in the distant parts; it holds many falajes, water springs, rock formations, medicinal herbs and archaeological inscriptions on stones and old houses.
Al Awabi is noted for extraordinary rock formations and high mountains.
Al Awabi is a wilayat of the Al Batinah South Governorate of Oman.

rejectedClaims: Rock ages anywhere between the two ends of the wadi. Only the entrance and the distant parts are published, so the interior profile used in the project is a set of teaching values and is labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A gradient in millions of years per kilometre presented as a fact. The 19.6 figure is derived on the page purely to be shown wrong, and is never stated as a property of the valley.
A population for the wilayat. The 2020 census figure was not traced to a primary table in this session, so none appears and the page argues from the valley instead.

coding-classes-in-mahout.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from distance rather than curriculum: Al Wusta is vast and thinly populated, so the range of subjects any settlement can staff is small, and a connection breaks the link between what a learner may study and how far they can travel.
coding-classes-in-mahout.localProject: A quantity with no single value, published as one. Barr Al Hikman is intertidal, so across one cycle the exposed area runs from 140 to 520 square kilometres, a factor of 3.7; the mean of 315 matches none of the thirteen hourly readings, making the average a state the place is never in, and any single published figure is right for roughly 8 per cent of the day. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Barr al Hikman is a peninsula in the northeast of Al Wusta Governorate bordering the sands to the north, the Masirah Channel to the east, the Gulf of Masirah to the south and Hashish Bay to the southwest; it is one of the most prominent coastal wetland regions in the Middle East, with a coastline of over 160 km bordered by an inland sabkha, and is a haven to nearly half a million waterbirds in winter.
Mahout is a wilayat of the Al Wusta Governorate of Oman.
Hufnat Beach is a destination within Mahout.

rejectedClaims: Any area figure for Barr Al Hikman. No hourly or reference-state survey was traced, so the thirteen readings in the project are teaching values and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ. The page deliberately publishes no single area, which is its own argument.
A single population figure for the wilayat. One reference gives 17,422 for 2020 and a population database gives 17,385 for the same census; neither is adopted here.
An exact coastline length. The published figure is over 160 km, kept as a lower bound.
A precise waterbird count. The published wording is nearly half a million in winter and both the hedge and the season are kept.

coding-classes-in-thumrait.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the town's position rather than from curriculum: a place people pass through rather than set out for tends to accumulate traffic without accumulating institutions, and teaching over a connection needs nothing built here first.
coding-classes-in-thumrait.localProject: The intermediate stops lost in an origin-destination table. Across six full itineraries Thumrait is the second busiest node, appearing in five, and an endpoints-only table records it zero times; five places vanish from the network entirely and 54 per cent of all node-visits disappear while every row stays true. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Thumrait is a small town and wilayat of the Dhofar Governorate in southern Oman, classified under the Koppen scheme as a subtropical desert climate.
Thumrait was historically an essential stop on the Arabian caravan routes, serving as a hub for the trade of frankincense, spices and other valuable commodities.
Thumrait is famed for Al Taghrooda, traditional chanted poetry composed and recited by men travelling on camel back through the desert, and is written about as a symbol of desert beauty.

rejectedClaims: Any specific caravan journey or route record. The six itineraries in the project are illustrative of how travel across the interior works, not records of particular trips, and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A population for the wilayat. The 2020 census figure was not traced to a primary table in this session, so none appears.
A road distance between Thumrait and anywhere else. None was verified, so no distance is stated.

coding-classes-in-mirbat.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the working day rather than from curriculum: where the fleet sails before dawn and is back by mid-morning, the hours a family can give to a lesson are unusual ones, and agreeing a slot is easier when nobody has to travel to reach it.
coding-classes-in-mirbat.localProject: The day boundary moves when you change clock. Oman runs at UTC+4, so of twelve pre-dawn boat departures between 02:40 and 06:45 local, four (33 per cent) fall on the previous day once converted. The date loses four departures and the day before gains four it never saw, so weekly totals reconcile perfectly while every daily figure is wrong. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Mirbat is a town on the eastern coastline of Dhofar, once a thriving port and trading hub, keeping historic architecture, tranquil beaches, traditional markets and coastal cliffs; fishing remains important and the harbour holds traditional wooden dhows, with fishermen unloading fresh catches along the waterfront.

Mohammed Bin Ali died in 556H, given as 1161 AD, came originally from Tarim in Hadhramaut in Yemen, moved to Mirbat and set up religious institutions, and is referred to by the title Sahib e Mirbat, the Master of Mirbat.
Mirbat is presented among the principal attractions of the Dhofar coast near Salalah.

rejectedClaims: Any actual departure log. No harbour record was found, so the twelve times in the project are teaching values chosen to span an ordinary pre-dawn window and are labelled as such in the project steps, the pitfalls note and the FAQ.
A conversion between the Hijri and Gregorian dates for the scholar. Both 556H and 1161 AD are quoted as the source gives them, side by side, and no arithmetic is performed on either.
A population for the wilayat. The 2020 census figure was not traced to a primary table in this session, so none appears.

coding-classes-in-masirah.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. The page argues from the crossing rather than from curriculum: anything an island learner cannot get on the island requires a boat and a day, and a lesson delivered over a connection removes that from the decision entirely.
coding-classes-in-masirah.localProject: Latitude and longitude read in the wrong order. The island is published at 20.47111 north, 58.81528 east; transposed it becomes 58.81528 north, 20.47111 east, which is open water in the Baltic Sea 5,246 km away. Every cheap validation passes: both values are in legal range, the hemisphere is unchanged, and the point is at sea, which for an island is what a reviewer wants to confirm. Only a bounding box on Oman's real extent of roughly 16 to 26 degrees north catches it. Assigned to this page and no other.

sources.claim: Masirah Island is at 20 degrees 28 minutes 16 seconds north, 58 degrees 48 minutes 55 seconds east, has an area of 649 square kilometres, stretches 95 km north to south and is between 12 and 14 km wide, and forms one of the provinces of Ash Sharqiyah South Governorate.

All of Oman's five turtle species visit the island or its waters, namely the green turtle, the loggerhead, the hawksbill, the olive ridley and the leatherback, and the island hosts the world's largest population of nesting loggerhead sea turtles.
Winds at the island are consistent and reach 20 to 45 knots especially from May through September, making it a noted kitesurfing destination.

rejectedClaims: A population figure. One reference gives 13,902 for 2020 and a population database gives 13,874 for the same census; both appear on the page and neither is adopted.
An annual turtle count. Figures circulate but none was verified at a primary source in this session, so no total appears and the page uses only the species list and the loggerhead nesting claim.
The identity of the sea the swapped coordinate lands in, beyond that it is open water in the Baltic. The distance of 5,246 km is computed from the published coordinates rather than looked up.

coding-classes-in-wadi-bani-khalid.market: Wadi Bani Khalid, Ash Sharqiyah North
coding-classes-in-wadi-bani-khalid.curriculumAuthority: Oman Ministry of Education, General Education Diploma. coding-classes-in-wadi-bani-khalid.localProject: Measuring only the part you can walk to. Of ten pools running up the wadi, four are reachable without a scramble; their mean depth is 1.77 m against a true 3.80 m across all ten, understating by 53 per cent, and the deepest pool ever measured is 2.6 m against a real deepest of 6.9 m. Every reading is accurate and the sample is the shallow 40 per cent. Distinct from non-response bias, which is the subject declining rather than the measurer not arriving. Assigned to this page and no other.

coding-classes-in-amstelveen.localProject: Stock versus flow. Statistics Netherlands published that non-EU knowledge migrants fell from 26 thousand (2022) to 14 thousand (2025), Indian migrants falling most, AND that four-year retention of Indian arrivals rose from 33 percent (2011 cohort) to 56 percent (2019 cohort). A learner builds a cohort model (stock = sum over cohorts of arrivals times retention) and shows that with arrivals indexed 100 to 54 the resident stock still rises 24 percent under the newer retention and stalls under the older one. Distinct from survivorship bias (Al Hail), from cumulative totals (Seria) and from the exposure-window trap on the Netherlands hub: the flaw here is reading a flow as a stock. Computed before writing; illustrative arrivals series labelled as such.

coding-classes-in-amsterdam.localProject: Two instruments, one disagreement rate. The city research office reports a doorstroomtoets result above the school advice for about one in five Amsterdam pupils against nearly one in three nationally (33 percent in Zuidoost, 30 in Noord, 20 citywide). A learner simulates 300,000 pupils with one true level, a school advice with a teacher tendency plus noise, and a test with its own noise, both banded, and finds that 33 percent arises from teachers 0.20 sd low with moderate test noise OR from unbiased teachers with high test noise, and ~20 percent from precise tests OR from teachers slightly high. The rate cannot identify the cause; only a third measurement can. Distinct from observation bias (Texas: the instrument changed over time), from metric definition (New Jersey) and from the Amstelveen stock/flow model. Simulation run before writing; all four table rows are labelled as a model.

coding-classes-in-eindhoven.localProject: Compounding uncertainty in a chain of ratios (a Fermi chain presented as a point). The one published figure is 20,000 workplaces at BIC Noord (Metropoolregio Eindhoven letter, 12 March 2026; council approval 10 March 2026). Homes inside Eindhoven = 20,000 x share of jobs going to newcomers / employed people per new household x share settling inside the municipality. Three plausible ratios multiplied together span a factor of six. Distinct from the ratio-of-ratios trap (Al Mouj), from a denominator nobody published (Bidbid), from a bound treated as a value (Hong Kong) and from the unit-of-analysis trap (Haima): the flaw here is presenting the product of unstated ranges as one number. coding-classes-in-almere.localProject: A height without its datum is not a number (reference-frame confusion, with a fixed datum against a moving reference). Almere lies 2 to 5 m below NAP; NAP descends from the 1684 Amsterdams Peil and Rijkswaterstaat says 0 m NAP is only approximately mean North Sea level; Deltares measured mean sea level at 11 cm above NAP in 2017, rising about 20 cm a century since 1890. coding-classes-in-rotterdam.localProject: Two units, one flow, opposite signs. Port of Rotterdam Authority 2025 figures (reported 27 February and 2 March 2026): containers 14.2 million TEU, plus 3.1 percent, while container cargo by weight fell 0.2 percent; total throughput 428.4 million tonnes, minus 1.7 percent. A TEU counts box-lengths including empties; a tonne weighs contents. The learner keeps the two as separate variables, derives 2024 TEU (13.77 million) and the weight-per-box index (96.8, minus 3.2 percent), then adds the unpublished empty share as a labelled assumption (20 to 23 percent: loaded boxes minus 0.8 percent; 20 to 25 percent: minus 3.3 percent). Distinct from the truncation trap (Yanqul: same unit, rounding), from the name-based misfiling of tonnages (Liwa), from the unit-of-analysis trap (Haima: one entity, two boundaries) and from the two-instruments trap (Amsterdam: two measurements of one latent value): the flaw here is reading growth in one unit as growth in the flow. Computed before writing; illustrative rows labelled.

coding-classes-in-gelderland.localProject: The ecological trap: a group attribute that no member of the group has. Gelderland is split between two school-holiday regions along a line between Apeldoorn and Arnhem (Rijksoverheid), and a published table assigns each municipality, with Montferland (Didam) and Neder-Betuwe (Dodewaard) split inside their own boundaries; the table also still names seven municipalities merged away since (Geldermalsen, Lingewaal, Neerijnen, Groesbeek, Ubbergen, Millingen aan de Rijn, Rijnwaarden). The learner tags 51 rows, computes a population-weighted provincial holiday, finds no school that keeps it, descends to municipality level (true for 49 of 51) and then to former-municipality level. Distinct from the weekend-as-input trap (Brunei: a calendar assumption in a date function), from the boundary-moved trap (Mahdah) and from the Zuid-Holland no-boundary trap: the flaw here is a value aggregated to a level at which it does not exist. Computed before writing; the dated names in the table are stated.

coding-classes-in-overijssel.localProject: A return period is a rate, not a countdown (per-year probability read as a schedule; compounding over a horizon). The pre-2017 dike standards from the published list of dike rings: 1 in 10,000 (Holland coast), 1 in 4,000 (Texel, Friesland and Groningen, Flevoland, Wieringermeer), 1 in 2,000 and 1 in 1,250 (river areas; dike rings 48 Rijn en IJssel and 49 IJsselland at 1 in 1,250). The learner restates each as p per year and compounds 1 minus (1 minus p)^N: 1 in 1,250 is 0.08 percent in a year, 2.37 over 30, 3.92 over 50, 6.20 over 80; 1 in 10,000 is 0.80 over 80. Distinct from base rates and conditional probability (Georgia), from class imbalance (Illinois) and from the bound-versus-value trap (Hong Kong): the flaw here is reading a per-year rate as a period, with no memory and no compounding. Computed before writing; the 2017 replacement standards were not available and are not stated.

coding-classes-in-delft.localProject: Ask whether the doubt is in the measurement or in the definition of the set. Between 34 and 37 paintings are attributed to Vermeer, and the range is not a counting error: the criterion is agreed and two or three specific canvases are disputed, so no better inventory closes it. The range propagates, giving 1.55 to 1.68 paintings a year across the roughly twenty-two years between his entry to the guild of Saint Luke in December 1653 and his burial on 15 December 1675. The learner models membership as a status field, returns a low and a high, names the disputed items and lets derived figures inherit the range. Distinct from the bound-versus-value trap (Hong Kong) and from ranking under measurement noise (Breda): here the quantity is fixed and knowable in principle, and the irreducible uncertainty is about which items belong to the set rather than about how well anything was measured. The range is quoted from the source and never narrowed.

coding-classes-in-emmen.curriculumAuthority: City and municipality of Emmen, Drenthe: 109,881 residents (CBS 2026) across 346.26 km2 at a published density of 327, the widest and thinnest ground of the Drenthe pages; 50,573 households averaging 2.12 with 18,480 single-person; 27,388 residents aged 65 and over against 27,412 under 25, twenty-four apart; 51 primary establishments (8,479 pupils) and 8 secondary (6,297), so about 166 pupils to a primary establishment; only 1,408 students at institutions here against 2,400 residents enrolled in higher education. coding-classes-in-emmen.localProject: Ask what the first observation is an observation of. Wildlands Adventure Zoo drew 1.3 million visitors in its openingsjaar and 951,000 in 2024, which reads as a fall of 27 percent, but 2016 measured curiosity about a park nobody had seen and the published series gives eight further years: 1,000,000 in 2017, 850,000 in 2018, 930,000 in 2019, 558,000 in 2020, 516,000 in 2021, 830,000 in 2022, 926,000 in 2023. Measured from 2018 the same 951,000 is a rise of 12 percent and from 2019 a rise of 2 percent, so the baseline chooses the conclusion. A second layer sits in the word openingsjaar, which does not say whether it covers the calendar year or the first twelve months: 1.3 million over the 289 days from 18 March 2016 is about 4,498 a day and over a full year about 3,562, against about 2,598 a day in 2024, making the fall 42 percent or 27 percent by reading. Distinct from the base-year trap (Flevoland), which is about choosing among many valid base years and dividing by zero, and from mismatched vintages (Apeldoorn): here every figure comes from one source and one series, and the defect is that the first point was generated by a different process from the rest while 2020 and 2021 were generated by closure. The learner names what made the first observation possible, converts to a per-day rate, marks the unusable years inside the data and reports the whole series with a declared baseline.

coding-classes-in-deventer.curriculumAuthority: City and municipality of Deventer, Overijssel: 105,111 residents (CBS 2026) on 134 km2 at a published density of 799; 48,940 households averaging 2.09 with 19,715 single-person, 40 percent; 35 primary establishments (8,388 pupils) and 10 secondary (5,088); 8,586 students at institutions here against 3,830 residents enrolled in higher education, so the municipality is a net importer of students, the opposite shape to Emmen. coding-classes-in-deventer.localProject: Ask whether the thing moved or the conditions moved. The Deventer book market drew 130,000 visitors in 2008 and 75,000 in 2009, a fall of 42 percent, and the entry states the cause outright: met 75.000 bezoekers was de editie 2009 vanwege de regen de slechtst bezochte in jaren. Nothing about the market changed, since it still ran to ruim 6 kilometer markt with circa 875 kramen, and the 2008 figure was matched again in 2014. Attendance is a stand-in produced jointly by the thing and the circumstances of measurement, so a move in it must be attributed before it is explained, and the stable measures (length, stall count) are the ones the weather cannot touch. A second layer: the market is held once a year on the first Sunday of August, so each annual observation is a single day with no averaging, and the conditions of that day pass through at full strength. Distinct from the launch-baseline trap (Emmen), where the first point comes from a different process, and from the cross-field validation trap (Den Bosch): here every value is correct, the series is internally consistent, and the defect is that the metric is confounded by something outside the thing it names. The source hedges (ruim, circa, zo'n) are reproduced rather than resolved.

coding-classes-in-venlo.curriculumAuthority: City and municipality of Venlo, Limburg: 104,195 residents (CBS 2026) on 128.99 km2 against the German border at a published density of 838; 49,770 households averaging 2.06 with 19,864 single-person, 40 percent; 29 primary establishments (8,281 pupils) and only 4 secondary (4,924), about 1,231 pupils to a secondary establishment; 3,248 students at institutions here against 2,900 residents enrolled; 7 woonplaatsen registered nationally against 10 places listed with populations by the municipal entry, both correct; stadsrechten 1343; mergers with Tegelen and Belfeld on 1 January 2001 and Arcen en Velden on 1 January 2010; Floriade 2012 and Brightlands Campus Greenport from 2017; regio Zuid holidays. coding-classes-in-venlo.localProject: Per capita is a sentence with a hidden subject: ask who the denominator is and whether they are the people the number is about. The municipal entry says Venlo receives jaarlijks circa 5 miljoen bezoekers uit voornamelijk het aangrenzende Ruhrgebied and that city-centre retail has been gebaat bij de bezoekers uit het Duitse achterland since the 1960s. Divided by 104,195 municipal residents that is about 48 visits per resident a year, by the 40,945 residents of the town itself about 122, and by 49,770 households about 100: three arithmetically correct figures, none of which describes anybody, because the visitors are not in any of those registers and the residents do not make the visits. The honest output is the raw count with the served population named, which is what the source itself does. Distinct from the denominator-choice trap (Gadong), where four nested resident populations are all defensible and the fault is failing to name which; from rate-versus-count (New York), where the denominator is right and only the ranking is wrong; and from the exposure-window trap (Emmen), where the denominator is unknown rather than mismatched. Here there is exactly one resident register, it is accurate, and it excludes the population the numerator was generated by. The source hedges circa and voornamelijk and the absence of a year are all preserved.
